Purpose: consistently create new insurance conversations without relying on luck.

Prospecting Sources

1. Referrals

Best source when someone who knows me introduces me to another person.

Goal:

  • 2 referral outreaches per day

Preferred referral:

  • Referrer gives me the person's name
  • Referrer tells them I will be calling
  • Referrer gives me their phone number
  • I make the first contact

2. Targeted Prospects

Specific households that appear to be strong Farm Bureau prospects.

Examples:

  • High-value homes in Lowell / Ada / Cascade
  • Multiple vehicles
  • Significant assets
  • Older / established households
  • Households that appear financially established
  • People with connections to other desirable households

Goal:

  • 3 targeted prospects per day

For each prospect:

  1. Identify the household
  2. Determine why they may be a good fit
  3. Determine how I can reach them
  4. Make an actual attempt to start a conversation
  5. If they engage, add them to Opportunity Pipeline

3. Cold Calling

Fully controllable outbound activity.

Goal:

  • 30 calls per day minimum
  • 50 calls = stretch goal

Possible sources:

  • Purchased / pulled public lists
  • Local business / household data
  • Registry information
  • Other legally usable prospect lists

Rule: Do not confuse building a list with making calls.

The list exists to create conversations.

4. Mail Campaigns

Use targeted prospect lists to support physical mail campaigns.

Purpose:

  • Create familiarity
  • Support cold calling
  • Reach prospects who do not answer
  • Build local agency recognition

Mailing is a supporting activity, not a replacement for direct prospecting.

5. Social / Community

Use Facebook and local community presence to create familiarity and inbound opportunities.

Purpose:

  • Become recognizable locally
  • Demonstrate expertise
  • Create reasons for people to contact me
  • Support referral and prospecting activity

Social media should not consume prime selling hours.

Prospecting Rules

Rule 1

A prospect is not valuable until I attempt to contact them.

Rule 2

Research should be brief and purposeful.

Rule 3

Every positive response becomes an opportunity in Opportunity Pipeline.

Rule 4

Every opportunity must have a next action and due date.

Rule 5

Do not hide from selling by improving the system.

The system exists to help me sell.

Targeted Prospect Standard

A targeted prospect is NOT simply someone whose name we have.

A targeted prospect is someone with enough evidence that an insurance conversation is worth initiating.

Possible signals:

  • Strong household or asset profile
  • Multiple vehicles
  • High-value home
  • Multiple properties
  • Business ownership
  • Significant recreational assets
  • Professional or executive household
  • Established household
  • Strong local/community connection
  • Existing personal relationship
  • Evidence they may be poorly served by their current insurance
  • Other reason to believe the household could be a strong opportunity

Project 200 is a source of potential prospects, not a prospect list.

Goal: identify 3 genuinely worthwhile targeted prospects per day.

AI should help research, filter, and prioritize candidates. The agent makes the final decision about whether someone is worth contacting.

Lead Selection Rules

Primary Target

High-quality homeowners in Kent County who appear likely to value strong insurance protection rather than simply chasing the lowest price.

Preferred Areas

  • Ada
  • Cascade
  • East Grand Rapids
  • Lowell
  • Other strong Kent County markets

Preferred Characteristics

  • Homeowner
  • Established household
  • Higher-value property or significant assets
  • Multiple vehicles
  • Multiple properties
  • Lakefront or recreational property
  • Boat / recreational vehicles
  • Successful professional or business owner
  • Strong community or referral connections
  • Newer or well-maintained home
  • Neighborhood/subdivision with potential referral opportunities
  • Evidence that the household may value quality coverage

Ownership Requirement

Prefer individually owned residential properties.

Avoid when possible:

  • LLCs
  • Corporations
  • Investment properties
  • Property management companies
  • Clearly commercial ownership
  • Trusts when the actual individual decision-maker cannot reasonably be identified

Contactability Requirement

A prospect is substantially more valuable if a reliable phone number can be identified.

A name and address alone does not make someone a high-priority cold-call prospect.

Unverified phone numbers are acceptable for calling.

Daily Lead Selection

The Lead List is the source pool.

Each day, select the highest-priority prospects from this list for the:

Targeted Prospect Queue

The goal is to create actual callable prospects, not simply accumulate names.

Priority Order

  1. Strong homeowner + strong household/asset profile + reliable contact information
  2. Strong homeowner + strong household/asset profile + phone number can reasonably be found
  3. Good property/household profile but contact information requires additional research
  4. Weak fit or questionable ownership
  5. Poor fit — do not spend prime calling time

Cold Call Rules

Cold calling target:

Minimum: 30 calls/day

Stretch: 50 calls/day

Focus on quality homeowners rather than low-value households.

The goal is not to find people who are merely willing to talk.

The goal is to find people who are:

  • Good insurance prospects
  • Financially capable of buying appropriate coverage
  • Likely to value protection
  • Potentially capable of becoming strong multi-policy customers
  • Potential referral sources

Lead List Philosophy

A large list is useful only if it produces callable prospects.

Do not confuse:

"We know their name"

with:

"This is someone worth calling."

The Lead List should continuously improve as prospects are researched, contacted, scored, and either promoted or discarded.

Outcome Definitions

No Answer — No Voicemail

  • No one answered
  • No voicemail left
  • Maximum attempts: 7

No Answer — Voicemail Left

  • No one answered
  • Voicemail was left
  • Maximum voicemails: 3

Bad Phone Number

  • Disconnected, invalid, or unusable number

Definitely Not Interested

  • Clearly hostile, rude, or unequivocally wants no contact

Not at This Time

  • Not interested right now, but not a hard rejection
  • Examples: recently renewed, bad timing, wants to revisit later
  • Follow up in 1 month
  • Then again in 2 months

Somewhat Interested

  • Interested enough to allow a quote
  • Has provided enough information to create an account and quote:
    • First and last name
    • Date of birth
    • Address
  • Does not necessarily want an insurance review

Hot Lead — Very Interested

  • Strong buying signal
  • Wants to see what I can do
  • Significant insurance pain or recent change
  • Open to moving forward

Insurance Review Scheduled

  • Agreed to an actual in-person insurance review / quote meeting

Source: Granola meeting notes. Attendee: Zach Hayes.

Mindset and the Four P's

  • Four P's framework: People, Process, Product, Purpose/Passion
  • People (prospects) come first: without someone willing to meet, nothing else matters
  • Sale number one: selling yourself that you can do this
  • Sale number two: convincing people to give you a chance
  • Sale number three: the actual product, only after trust is built
  • Never conflate selling the appointment with selling insurance — sell the appointment only; sell insurance once you're on it
  • Process matters as much as product: selling yourself, the company, and your ideas during the fact find
  • A confused buyer never buys: keep it simple
  • Product is the least important P: it's just the final solution to uncovered problems
  • Purpose and passion: sales is the transfer of belief — if you don't believe in what you're selling, it shows
  • Life insurance described as a "mission field": creating something for families no one else had

Blue Ocean vs. Red Ocean

  • Auto and home = red ocean: heavy competition, existing agents, carriers, prices — must convince clients to break up with current agent and carrier
  • Life insurance = blue ocean: rarely replacing anything, competing only against mindset
  • Most people are severely underinsured
  • The sale is simply: here's what you'd need if you died, here's what you have, here's the gap

The Life Insurance Sales Process Today

  • Modern process is application-first, not product-first — too many rate tiers, health variables, and products to quote upfront
  • Never give a price estimate before underwriting: sets wrong expectations (e.g., quote $35/month, client gets table-rated to $110, now they feel misled)
  • Step 1: build the need, get agreement there's a gap
  • Step 2: submit application to establish rate and confirm insurability
  • Step 3: once approved, design the product mix and present options
  • Underwriting timeline: typically 2–4 weeks, up to 4–6 if doctor records needed
  • Client must answer the vendor's phone call promptly for the telephone interview
  • Paramedic exam (blood, urine, height/weight) usually done at client's home
  • Coach clients upfront to move quickly through the process
  • Right Life app (18–54, max $500K): can skip phone interview and paramedic, but limited
  • Full underwriting preferred for most cases: cleaner, more thorough, fewer follow-ups
  • Electronic Part B (client self-fills health questions) generates more agent follow-up vs. telephone interview

Handling Objections and Smokescreens

  • Most objections are smokescreens: "need to think about it," "can't afford it"
  • People have money for what they want to spend it on
  • If you get many smokescreens, you likely didn't educate them well enough
  • Dad's rule: either you sell them on why they must, or they sell you on why they can't
  • Goal: 5 life insurance pivots per week — expect roughly 1 idiot, 1 unresolvable objection, 2–3 workable prospects, 1–2 who take action
  • Both spouses must be present for the life insurance conversation — one spouse cannot explain it as well; the absent one will stall

Term Insurance: Products and Structure

  • ~85% of policies placed are term; 15% whole life
  • Term is a pure cost: premium disappears unless there's a death, like auto insurance
  • Premium factors: death benefit size, health/habits, sex (females pay less), age
  • Age is the one constant: cost rises as age increases, exponentially after 50s
  • Level term products:
    • ART (5-year level term): rare, used by new agents, business equipment loans, or smokers planning to quit
    • T10: second most popular, cheapest, good for short-term needs
    • T20: most popular, the "Swiss Army knife," not too short or long
    • T30: third most popular, highest income protection, guaranteed for full 30 years
    • Term to 70: niche product, 35–60 issue age, fills gap between T10 and T20 for mid-50s clients
    • Return of Premium T20: 4–5x the cost of T20; rarely recommended
  • At end of level period, price spikes to unaffordable: the "special gift"
  • Match term length to the actual need being protected
  • Layering strategy: stack a T10, T20, T30 (and optionally whole life) to align coverage with life stages
    • Example: T10 for kids leaving home, T20 for mortgage, T30 to retirement
  • DPW (Disability Premium Waiver): always add this rider on every eligible policy
    • Waives premium if client becomes totally and permanently disabled during the level period
    • Eligible ages 15–55; premium drops at age 61 when rider falls off
    • On whole life: waiver continues for life if disabled before age 60
  • Minimum policy: $100K for most terms; ART minimum is $250K
  • Always sell at least $125K if client wants the smallest possible term — allows a $25K partial conversion while retaining $100K term

Term Conversion to Permanent

  • All terms are convertible to whole life with no health questions
  • Convertible after 12 months in force, through the level period or to age 65, whichever comes first
  • Best time to convert: as early as possible, it only gets more expensive with age
  • Partial conversions allowed: minimum $100K per conversion
    • Example: converted $1M term in four partial conversions, each reducing remaining term face amount
  • Conversion is a key ongoing conversation with existing clients

Whole Life: Select vs. Premier

  • Whole life basics: guaranteed death benefit, guaranteed cash value (grows to equal death benefit at age 100), guaranteed level premium
  • Two types:
    • Select Whole Life: non-participating (minimal dividends), lower premium, robust reduced paid-up option
    • Premier Whole Life: participating, higher premium, robust dividend scale — after ~20 years, dividend can exceed the annual premium, effectively making the policy self-funding
  • Select Whole Life illustrated (Joe, age 40, $100K, non-tobacco preferred):
    • Monthly premium: $110.59 (including DPW); premium drops at age 61 when DPW falls off
    • Cash value reaches $100K at age 100 (guaranteed)
    • Minimal dividends (~$5–$15/year): negligible on plain policy
  • Reduced Paid-Up option (Select):
    • At age 70 (30 years in): can go paid-up with ~$76K death benefit, zero future premiums
    • Cash continues to grow to equal the reduced death benefit at age 100
    • "If clients know there's a way out, they're more willing to get in"

Paid-Up Addition Rider (PUAR)

  • Best rider available: every dollar deposited goes almost entirely to cash value and paid-up death benefit
  • Must be added at policy inception: cannot be added later
  • Life Solutions software forces a PUAR selection when illustrating Select Whole Life
  • Deposit options: None / Minimum ($100/year, $8.33/month) / One times base premium / Maximum (three times base, rarely used) / Other (custom amount)
  • PUAR deposit is flexible: can be raised or lowered after issue, or removed entirely
  • Illustrated effect (Joe, age 40, $100K + $39.41/month PUAR):
    • At age 70: paid-up addition death benefit adds ~$45K on top of base $100K
    • Paid-up addition cash value adds ~$26K on top of base cash value
    • Reduced paid-up at age 70 becomes ~$121K (vs. $76K without PUAR)
  • Recommendation: put minimum PUAR on every Select Whole Life policy unless there's a reason not to

Selling Concepts and Presentation Techniques

  • "Sparks" framework from a speaking course: use stories and drawings to make concepts vivid
  • Draw the term insurance diagram live with clients: premium box, cost curve, level term lines
  • Stories create emotional engagement; drawings create visual memory
  • Black Swan concept: "The unknown will never be known, but you can envision what it happening would look like, and that should be the basis for all your decisions today"
    • Applied to life insurance: walk clients through their own death story — what would they want to happen? What would it cost? How much do they have? What's the gap?
  • LIF(E) calculation: structured need-building tool (covered later in the day)
    • Debt payoff, final expenses, income replacement, education, weddings, down payments
  • Obituary habit: reading obituaries reinforces purpose and reminds of the mission
  • Commission breath: clients sense it; lead with genuine care for the family's outcome

Annuities, Asset Protection, and Priorities

  • Annuities not covered in first 30 days: no multiplier, doesn't count toward contract
  • Asset Protection / Trust Advisor seminar: September 2nd, full afternoon session
  • Product priority pyramid (beginner staples): auto, home, umbrella, life; annuities and other products come later
  • Age of Business seminar: Kellogg Center, includes 2027 Marketing Planning Guide and breakout sessions
  • Marketing co-op program: company helps fund community partnerships up to a dollar threshold
  • Personal life insurance policies: agents paid 2.0 month final business in year one
    • Policy count credit applies for first 8 months only; commission always applies
    • Life changes (marriage, new baby) allow additional personal policy count exceptions

Next Steps

  • Apply for personal life insurance policies — go through the process firsthand so you can explain it fluently to clients; consider running one through telephone interview and one through electronic Part B to compare
  • Attend Life Solutions system training at Portage tomorrow morning — walk through a full life application start to finish, including amendments and product design after approval
  • Review the paper Turbo app and Right Life application tonight — familiarize with the questions so the pivot from PNC to life application feels natural face-to-face
  • Register for the Asset Protection / Trust Advisor seminar (September 2nd) — full afternoon on annuities and asset protection planning

Source: Granola meeting notes. Attendee: Zach Hayes.

Life Insurance Product Overview

  • Term policy lengths: 5-year (ART), 10, 20, 30-year; plus Term to 72 (T72)
  • Most popular: T20, then T10; together ~90–95% of sales
  • ART: annual renewable after 5-year level period; minimum face $25K (vs. $100K for all other terms)
  • Minimum issue age: 18; maximum: 85 (T72 max: 50)
  • All terms except T72 are convertible
  • Must be in force at least 1 year before converting
  • Convertible until end of level term period or age 65, whichever comes first
  • Partial conversion allowed: must retain at least $100K in term
  • Terms issued to age 67+ are never convertible (but whole life was available at time of approval)

Whole Life Products

  • Three products: Select, Premier, Single Premium (rare, ~1%)
  • Select: non-participating (no dividends); robust reduced paid-up option; minimum $25K face
  • Premier: participating (dividend-paying); dividend typically covers premium by year 20–21; minimum $100K face
  • Both issue from age 0 to 85
  • All whole life policies can convert to reduced paid-up if client stops paying — base policy reduces; paid-up addition (PUA) rider death benefit is retained

Paid-Up Addition Rider (PUAR)

  • Must be added at policy inception; cannot be added later
  • Minimum: $8.33/month or $100/year
  • Options: minimum, 1x base premium, or specified amount
  • Grows the death benefit and cash value over time
  • On Select: strongly recommend always including PUAR (low barrier, big long-term impact)
  • On Premier: dividend already buys PUAs; PUAR optional but accelerates cash value and can shorten premium-paying period to ~10 years

Disability Premium Waiver (DPW)

  • "Never event" rider: put it on every eligible life policy
  • Waives premium if insured becomes disabled, for the remaining term of the policy
  • On term: protects through the end of the level period (not necessarily to age 60)
  • On whole life: waives premium for life of policy
  • Not available on single premium policies (no premium to waive)

Term vs. Permanent: Client Explanation

  • Term = pure cost; premium disappears to home office — money reappears only at death (within the term), paid to beneficiaries
  • Analogy: renting vs. buying a house; term is renting, whole life builds equity
  • Whole life = cost + investment; cash value builds over time
  • Other cost-only insurance analogies: auto, home (money reappears only on a claim)
  • Cost drivers: age, health, habits, face amount
  • Premium increases with age (slowly when young, steeply later); level terms average out that rising cost over the period

Structuring Term Policies (Laddering)

  • Match term length to the actual need; don't over- or under-insure
  • Common mistake: agents selling only T10 (cheapest) — client likely pays more in the long run
  • Layering example for a 34-year-old with 9- and 7-year-olds:
    • Option A: $1.5M 30-year term, $92.50/month, total paid $33,300; owns nothing at year 31
    • Option B: $500K T10 + $500K T20 + $500K T30; avg $60/month, total paid $21,601; coverage steps down as needs shrink
    • Option C: same as B plus $100K Premier Whole Life; avg $208/month, total paid ~$83,940; net cost ~$9,174 after $74,766 cash value; $200,950+ death benefit at age 61, growing to $325K+ at 80
  • Option B flexibility advantage: can drop individual policies in hardship; Option A is all-or-nothing
  • DPW on all three term policies in Option C: if disabled, all three run to full term with no premium

LAFE Framework (Needs Analysis)

  • L: Liabilities/Loans — pay off all household debt at death
  • A: (implied in income discussion)
  • F: Final Expenses — typically $25K–$50K; covers funeral, medical co-pays, time off, counseling
  • E: Everything Else — education, wedding, first home down payment, spoiling grandkids
  • I: Income Replacement
    • Ask: "How much would you want coming in monthly on your behalf?"
    • Common answers: full income or ~70% (deceased no longer needs car, food, clothing)
    • Follow-up: "For how many years?" — guide if answer seems too low relative to kids' ages
    • Three natural endpoints: youngest child out of college, spouse to retirement, or arbitrary number
  • Gap = LAFE total minus existing coverage; most clients have a significant gap
  • Work insurance is not owned insurance: if they change jobs, the benefit disappears

Sales Process and Scripting

  • Upfront contract (every call): "We want to make sure your home, your assets, and your family are protected" — sets expectation for life insurance conversation before it arises; no surprise pivot later
  • Pivot from P&C to life: "Where do you currently keep your life insurance?"
    • Common answers: work, nothing, don't believe in it
    • "Work" response: acknowledge, then distinguish owned vs. employer-provided coverage
  • Transition: "Let me run you through a quick exercise — it's an acronym called LAFE…"
  • Assume close: don't ask permission to proceed; move to application naturally — "To get started, I just need your driver's license"
  • All decision-makers must be present; missing the spouse is a critical failure point
  • 3% income rule (David Allard): frame the premium as 3% of income to solve the gap (on $100K income: ~$250/month; positions the cost as reasonable before showing options)
  • "Polite or honest?" reframe for objections (e.g., "I can't afford it")
  • Key principle: sales is a transfer of belief; make it the client's story, not yours

ABC Proposal Approach

  • Present 2–3 structured options; don't let clients design their own plan
    • Option A: single large term policy (simple, but inflexible; nothing at end)
    • Option B: laddered term (flexible, lower avg cost, multiple policy counts)
    • Option C: laddered term + Premier Whole Life (highest upfront, best long-term value)
  • Convertibility built into every review conversation: revisit 3–5 years in
  • Advanced planning partners (Frank Campioni, Jim Densey): bring in for large/complex cases; they take 20%, agent keeps 80%
  • Household policy count example: husband + wife (3 policies each) + 2 kids (1 each) = 8–10 policies per household
  • Target: 10–12 households/year → ~50 policies; requires ~5 fact finders/week

Commissions and Production

  • Term commission tiers: $500K+ = 50%; $250K–$499,999 = 40%
  • Premier Whole Life: 40%; Select Whole Life: 50%
  • Life commission paid as premium comes in (unlike P&C, which pays full-year commission upfront)
    • Annual pay: full first-year commission earned immediately
    • Monthly pay: commission earned only on months premium received in that calendar year
  • All American requirements (first 3 years): 35 policies + $11K first-year life commission, or 50 policies + $9K
  • New agent 2x multiplier: Option C example earns ~$1,200 base commission → $2,400 with multiplier = $3,600
    • Option C annual premium ~$2,700; company pays $3,600 in year 1 — net positive for new agents placing their own policy

Life Solutions System (Salesforce)

  • Access: Salesforce → right-hand menu → Life Solutions
  • Life New Business Activity: tracks all pending applications, underwriting status, approvals — check daily once apps are in flight
  • Status indicators: sent/reviewed (phone interview), received/not reviewed (paramed results)
  • Starting an application:
    • Enter name, DOB, sex; select term or whole life product
    • Rating class unknown until underwriting; don't pre-commit a class when illustrating
    • "Prior approval notification": check YES for large cases to hold approval and present options; check NO for straightforward child/simple policies
    • Apply for full gap amount as one policy; split into multiple policies via LG594 form after approval
    • Trial application: use only when known health issues exist; otherwise leave unchecked
    • Do not collect money on trial apps; conditional receipt only if placing coverage immediately
  • Key application fields: net worth (assets minus liabilities), annual income, existing coverage, primary care physician (Google address if needed)
  • Beneficiaries: always get Social Security numbers; spouse as primary, estate or children as contingent
  • Replacing existing coverage: answer "no" unless definitively replacing — avoids triggering replacement paperwork from other carriers
  • Paramedic exam: can let Farm Bureau coordinate (800-number) or agent controls via Beth (Paramed Solutions) — agent-controlled preferred: faster, more visibility, Beth texts clients directly
  • Agent report: separate from application; internal only; completed after app is locked
  • Signatures: client present = click through; client not present = DocuSign via email

Next Steps

  • Watch Steve Ellis training video — full sales process walkthrough from first call through life pivot; can be listened to in the car
  • Apply for personal life insurance through Life Solutions — go through underwriting now to know your own approval class and understand the client experience firsthand
  • Practice upfront contract and LAFE scripting — record yourself, use a mirror or significant other; goal is to have responses to "I have it through work" and "I can't afford it" off the tip of your tongue before client meetings
  • Attend Jumpstart Life training — scheduled for approximately the week of August 25th; will cover Life Solutions, underwriting, and illustrations in depth

net cost ~$9,174 after $74,766 cash value; $200,950+ death benefit at age 61, growing to $325K+ at 80 Option B flexibility advantage: can drop individual policies in hardship; Option A is all-or-nothing DPW on all three term policies in Option C: if disabled, all three run to full term with no premium LAFE Framework (Needs Analysis) L: Liabilities/Loans — pay off all household debt at death A: (implied in income discussion) F: Final Expenses — typically $25K–$50K; covers funeral, medical co-pays, time off, counseling E: Everything Else — education, wedding, first home down payment, spoiling grandkids I: Income Replacement Ask: "How much would you want coming in monthly on your behalf?" Common answers: full income or ~70% (deceased no longer needs car, food, clothing) Follow-up: "For how many years?" — guide if answer seems too low relative to kids' ages Three natural endpoints: youngest child out of college, spouse to retirement, or arbitrary number Gap = LAFE total minus existing coverage; most clients have a significant gap Work insurance is not owned insurance: if they change jobs, the benefit disappears Sales Process and Scripting Upfront contract (every call): "We want to make sure your home, your assets, and your family are protected" — sets expectation for life insurance conversation before it arises; no surprise pivot later Pivot from P&C to life: "Where do you currently keep your life insurance?" Common answers: work, nothing, don't believe in it "Work" response: acknowledge, then distinguish owned vs. employer-provided coverage Transition: "Let me run you through a quick exercise — it's an acronym called LAFE…" Assume close: don't ask permission to proceed; move to application naturally — "To get started, I just need your driver's license" All decision-makers must be present; missing the spouse is a critical failure point 3% income rule (David Allard): frame the premium as 3% of income to solve the gap (on $100K income: ~$250/month; positions the cost as reasonable before showing options) "Polite or honest?" reframe for objections (e.g., "I can't afford it") Key principle: sales is a transfer of belief; make it the client's story, not yours ABC Proposal Approach Present 2–3 structured options; don't let clients design their own plan Option A: single large term policy (simple, but inflexible; nothing at end) Option B: laddered term (flexible, lower avg cost, multiple policy counts) Option C: laddered term + Premier Whole Life (highest upfront, best long-term value) Convertibility built into every review conversation: revisit 3–5 years in Advanced planning partners (Frank Campioni, Jim Densey): bring in for large/complex cases; they take 20%, agent keeps 80% Household policy count example: husband + wife (3 policies each) + 2 kids (1 each) = 8–10 policies per household Target: 10–12 households/year → ~50 policies; requires ~5 fact finders/week Commissions and Production Term commission tiers: $500K+ = 50%; $250K–$499,999 = 40% Premier Whole Life: 40%; Select Whole Life: 50% Life commission paid as premium comes in (unlike P&C, which pays full-year commission upfront) Annual pay: full first-year commission earned immediately Monthly pay: commission earned only on months premium received in that calendar year All American requirements (first 3 years): 35 policies + $11K first-year life commission, or 50 policies + $9K New agent 2x multiplier: Option C example earns ~$1,200 base commission → $2,400 with multiplier = $3,600 Option C annual premium ~$2,700; company pays $3,600 in year 1 — net positive for new agents placing their own policy Life Solutions System (Salesforce) Access: Salesforce → right-hand menu → Life Solutions Life New Business Activity: tracks all pending applications, underwriting status, approvals — check daily once apps are in flight Status indicators: sent/reviewed (phone interview), received/not reviewed (paramed results) Starting an application: Enter name, DOB, sex; select term or whole life product Rating class unknown until underwriting; don't pre-commit a class when illustrating "Prior approval notification": check YES for large cases to hold approval and present options; check NO for straightforward child/simple policies Apply for full gap amount as one policy; split into multiple policies via LG594 form after approval Trial application: use only when known health issues exist; otherwise leave unchecked Do not collect money on trial apps; conditional receipt only if placing coverage immediately Key application fields: net worth (assets minus liabilities), annual income, existing coverage, primary care physician (Google address if needed) Beneficiaries: always get Social Security numbers; spouse as primary, estate or children as contingent Replacing existing coverage: answer "no" unless definitively replacing — avoids triggering replacement paperwork from other carriers Paramedic exam: can let Farm Bureau coordinate (800-number) or agent controls via Beth (Paramed Solutions) — agent-controlled preferred: faster, more visibility, Beth texts clients directly Agent report: separate from application; internal only; completed after app is locked Signatures: client present = click through; client not present = DocuSign via email Next Steps Watch Steve Ellis training video — full sales process walkthrough from first call through life pivot; can be listened to in the car Apply for personal life insurance through Life Solutions — go through underwriting now to know your own approval class and understand the client experience firsthand Practice upfront contract and LAFE scripting — record yourself, use a mirror or significant other; goal is to have responses to "I have it through work" and "I can't afford it" off the tip of your tongue before client meetings Attend Jumpstart Life training — scheduled for approximately the week of August 25th; will cover Life Solutions, underwriting, and illustrations in depth

Overview

  • Homeowner discounts reward: pay in full, automatic withdrawal, multiple policies (Auto/Life/Commercial), longevity with FB, accident-free, closing business before effective date
  • Agent is responsible for eligibility determination based on applicant info + visual inspection
  • Applies to Primary and Seasonal dwellings on Homeowners, Mobile Homeowners, Condo, or Renters policies
  • "Dwelling" = 1-4 family dwelling, mobile-manufactured housing unit, condo unit, apartment, or townhouse (primary or seasonal)

Peril Forms

Special Form — "open perils" for Dwelling (A) and Other Structures (B), subject to exclusions. Coverage C (Personal Property) stays Broad Form perils unless Special Personal Property endorsement (GH 66 10) is added.

Builders Risk

Hydroplanes, homemade/kit boats, houseboats, racing/tournament-fishing/stunt boats, >70 mph capability, sailboats racing for money, chartered watercraft, ferro cement boats, non-marine engines, under construction/repair/unrepaired damage, co-owned, rented to others, operator <14, operator born after 12-31-78 without Boater Safety Cert, fishing/skiing equipment (see Sports Equipment class instead), stored 50+ miles out of state.

  • Attached via GH 66 44 (Special Form) & GH 66 45 (Travel Trailer)
  • Special Form classes: watercraft (Sailboat/Personal Watercraft/Outboards/Inboards & I/O & Jet Boats), recreational vehicles, sports equipment (Firearms / Other-than-Firearms), electronic equipment, cell phones, medical devices, misc. property, jewelry
  • Building materials handled under Builders Risk, not SPA

Source: Homeowners System Guide 2025

New Submission Workflow

  1. Account → Actions → New Submission → set effective date → select Homeowners
  2. Important: if the policy will be Lien Billed (mortgagee billed), it must live on its own separate Guidewire account — no other policies on that account
  3. Offerings screen: pick Policy Type (Special, Broad, etc.) and Offering Selection. Once you navigate away, Policy Type cannot be changed — Offering Selection can still be edited later.

Qualification Screen

  • First 3 questions required to quote; 4th required to bind but not to quote
  • Best practice: complete all of them anyway. A disqualifying answer = hard stop

Policy Info Screen

  • Additional Named Insureds: must exist at Account level first
  • Affinity Discount: select the group, then indicate which named insured qualifies — proof may be required
  • FB Advantage Score: must be retrieved before leaving the screen if not already on file
  • Multi-Policy Discount: a Personal Auto submission number works while quoting, but the auto policy must be in force and its policy number entered before the HO policy can issue with the discount
  • Billing History / Advance Signing / Claim History: display-only

Dwelling Screen

Covers Census Tract, Protection Class, underwriting questions, and Additional Interests — complete as much as possible even though not all fields are required to quote.

Additional Interests / Mortgagees

  • Add → From Address Book → search by Company name → verify name/address before selecting
  • Only one "Mortgagee 1" interest type allowed per policy — adding two causes policy errors
  • If mortgagee billed, select Yes under "Send Billing to Additional Interest" — only the first mortgagee can be billed this way
  • Approved vs. unapproved mortgagees: check the "Approved Mortgagee" column when searching (Yes/No). Only approved mortgagees show up when marking "Send Billing to Additional Interest" = Yes.
  • Unapproved or not-found mortgagee: Add → New Company → fill required fields → Send Billing = Yes → quoting sends an activity to Agency Support for approval. Policy can be quoted but not bound until approved.
  • Once approved: you must edit and requote the submission to pull in the correct billing account before completing the activity — skipping this means billing won't set up correctly
  • Lien Bill HO on an account with other active policies = blocker. Move it to its own account.
  • Changing mortgagee mid-term: before the bill date, invoice reschedules to the new lienholder same month; after the bill date, it reschedules for the following month and any payment already received from the old lienholder gets returned by Customer Service

Dwelling Construction & RCT

  • RCT (Residential Component Technology) becomes available once Home Year, Home Style, Number of Families, Number of Stories, and Square Footage are entered
  • Not required to quote, but best practice to run it for accuracy
  • Not available for Renters; not required but recommended for Condo (calculates "bare walls-in" value)
  • Roofing upgrades: no contractor documentation needed — rated off Roof Year if provided, otherwise Year Built
  • Workflow: RCT Launch → review/edit each section (add Section/Wing for additions) → verify "SYS" (system-generated) fields → Calculate → Finish → Save/Close → back on Dwelling Construction, select Sync from RCT → Garage/Roof/Foundation Type populate
  • Repair Cost RCT (vs. Replacement Cost): after syncing, in RCT select Calculate → Options → Markups and Adjustments → enter age/condition → Finish/Save/Close → Sync from RCT again to pull Actual Cash Value → on Coverages screen set Loss Evaluation to Repair Cost
    • Dwelling Limit must be under 80% of the 100% Replacement Cost value and no less than 100% of Actual Cash Value — system auto-adjusts if you're outside that range

Coverages Screen

  • Dwelling $300k–$999,999 → default deductible $2,500; $1M+ → default deductible $5,000
  • Windstorm/Hail deductible can't be lower than Section I deductible; percentage options are 0.5/1/2/3/5% of Coverage A
  • Optional Liability and Optional Property Coverages only display if the policy qualifies
  • ACV Loss Evaluation for Roof (wind/hail damage): removing this requires underwriting approval
  • Additional Coverages tab is read-only — limits vary by offering (Base/Builders Risk vs. Select Plus vs. Select Premier)
  • PFAS Exclusion and War & Cyber Operation Exclusion are automatically included and cannot be removed
  • Modifiers tab: read-only summary of discounts/surcharges

Scheduled Personal Articles (SPA)

  • Items stored/located outside Michigan aren't covered unless within 50 miles of the residence
  • Add SPA Type → fill required fields (serial number not required to quote, but required before issuing)
  • Additional Interest on an SPA item: must exist at Account level first
  • SPA Operators (for watercraft etc.): pull existing FB auto policy drivers via policy number (format PA-XXXXXXXX), or manually add from existing account contacts — driver's license auto-populates if already on the contact
  • Removing: select the SPA class → Remove SPA (for one item), or select the whole SPA Type → Remove → confirm (for all items of that type)

Risk Analysis → Quote → Issue

  • Checklist tab: review early, ideally while first talking to the client (e.g. "photos of all sides of the dwelling required") — upload photos before requesting Underwriting approval
  • Prior Losses: required to issue — Retrieve Prior Loss, or manually add if needed
  • Run Validations before issuing to surface anything outstanding
  • Payment: if it's the first policy on the account, select Payment Type and due day — otherwise it inherits the account's existing billing setup
  • Lien Billed policies: Bind Options is disabled on every screen except Payment — you must issue from the Payment tab specifically
  • Signed application required — DocuSign accepted (note: the in-app "DocuSign It" button is currently broken; download and send via the DocuSign website instead). Upload as PC Application / Eligibility-Signature.

Field Issue Dec

  • Available once quoted and all underwriting approvals are complete
  • Lets you generate documentation before the closing date is confirmed — useful for mortgagee-billed purchases with an uncertain close date
  • Generates even if the mortgagee isn't approved yet
  • Print Field Issue Dec is unavailable while blockers exist — clear those first
  • Workflow: quote → sign page 1 → Fill & Sign page 2 with payment amount → save to H/S drive → send to the mortgage company → upload the completed form back to policy files

Quoting a mortgagee-billed HO with an unconfirmed closing date

  1. Quote the policy, give the client the number, don't bind yet
  2. Add a note: "Quoted new submission with Advance Signing Discount on [date]. Closing date estimated for [date] but not set — premium quoted $X."
  3. As the closing date firms up, add a UW Issue on Risk Analysis and request approval — Underwriting overrides to apply the correct Advance Signing Discount
  4. Once approved, bind/issue
  5. For the mortgage company: use the Guidewire submission number (not a bound policy number) on the Field Issued Declaration form — this lets the mortgage company pay without the policy being bound first, avoiding an unnecessary cancel-and-rewrite

Document Upload Quick Reference

ItemDocument TypeSub Type
Prior Proof of InsurancePC UnderwritingProof
EFT Authorization FormPC Home Office OnlyEFT
Statement of No LossesPC ReinstatementNo Losses
AppraisalPC UnderwritingAppraisal
Self-Review LetterPC CorrespondenceSelf-Review Letter
Driver Insured ElsewherePC UnderwritingProof

Manually Determining Protection Class

When it doesn't auto-populate: Barnyard → Online Manuals → Public Protection Class Manual → find the township/county → note the code. If it's a split class, open the HO/LE PPC Assignment Flowchart and answer the questions to land on the correct number, then select it manually on the Dwelling screen.

Manually Updating Census Tract

When it doesn't auto-populate: on the Location field, select New Location → use the Census Tract Mapping link → enter the full address → Search. If a match appears, note the tract code and select it in Guidewire. If no match appears, use User Select Tract and click the map at the correct location to generate a code instead.

Mid-Term Changes

  • Always add a note describing the change
  • Actions → Change Policy → set effective date
  • The Change Description field on Policy Summary may or may not print on the declarations — verify before assuming it's documented for the client

Renewals — Boeckh Factor

The Boeckh Factor (aka Inflation Guard / Construction Cost Adjustment Factor / Personal Property Adjustment Factor) auto-adjusts coverage limits at renewal based on location and effective date. Below 1.00 = decrease, above 1.00 = increase. Found on the Dwelling screen each renewal.

Policy TypeApplies To
Homeowners Special/BroadDwelling (A) automatically; Coverage C follows the same % if it was previously manually increased, otherwise auto-updates with the Dwelling limit
Mobile Home Special/BroadDoes not apply — factor always 1.00, limits only change if manually updated
RentersPersonal Property (C) only
CondoPersonal Property (C), and Dwelling (A) unless set to the basic $5,000 amount

Location Address Changes

Cannot be changed if the policyholder actually moved (except renters) — that requires a new policy. For typos/manual overrides: Actions → New Activity → Underwriting Review → Review and Approve, subject "Location Address Correction," describe the correct address and reason in the notes. Leave a matching note on the policy itself.

Underwriting Blockers — Best Practices

  • Send to Underwriting as the final step, once everything else is complete — reduces back-and-forth
  • Always add policy notes before submitting; blockers without supporting notes get sent back
  • Don't submit an incomplete application — it forces a second UW review and delays things further
  • Blockers are worked in the order received; if returned for missing info, it keeps its place in line once resubmitted — get it right the first time

Common Blockers Reference

BlockerTriggerWhat to Do
ACV for Roof (Wind/Hail)ACV loss evaluation added for roofUpload roof photos + a replacement timeline
Additional ResidenceNew residence added to policyUpload labeled photos, including any liability hazards
Additional Named Insured Insurable InterestANI is on the deed but doesn't occupy the homeShould be Additional Insured, not ANI/PNI — edit the contact type
Backdated TransactionEffective date >2 days in the pastInclude signed Statement of No Loss, or a signature dated on/before the effective date
Builders RiskAny builders risk policyList contractor name + construction start/finish dates
Business Pursuits — Annual ReceiptsReceipts over $30,000Verify this isn't the insured's primary income source
Open Claim, $0 amount / CLUE Claim Count (3+ in 36mo) / CLUE Open ClaimCLUE report findingsDetail the claim in policy notes: repairs completed, confirmation all repairs done, claim count
Condo Rented to OthersRented more than 6 weeks/yearNote weeks rented per year and whether it's listed on a home-sharing platform
Dwelling Increase Over $50,000Manual increase >$50kRun a new, complete RCT; submit photos if needed
Replacement Cost 200%+ of RCTDwelling limit far exceeds 100% RCT valueFull detailed RCT + written explanation for the gap
Effective Date >45 Days OutQuoted too far in advanceWait to submit until within 45 days of effective date
Farming or Business Activities"Yes" on that dwelling questionComplete the business question on the application
Marijuana Grow"Yes" on grow lights/hydroponics questionDetailed description on Qualification screen + photos of the operation

(Several more blockers exist in the full guide — Dwelling on an Island, Electric Heat Amps, Electrical System, Heat Distribution — these are informational only and require no field action; Underwriting reviews them automatically.)

Source: In-person session transcript, Cascade ADO. Trainer: Randi Tucker. Covers live product review + Guidewire quote demo not already captured in the other Homeowners notes.

Field Underwriting — What Agents Must Do

  • Agents (not a third-party vendor) take the photos and get eyes on the property — Farm Bureau deliberately kept this in-house rather than outsourcing to drone/inspection companies.
  • Required: photos of all sides of dwelling, any outbuildings/structures, liability hazards (junk piles, dead/leaning trees near the house), SPA items, heating units.
  • Handrail rule: any deck 2+ feet above grade, or any stairway with 3+ steps, needs a railing. Missing rail on an existing policy can trigger a cancellation notice.
  • Pools: in-ground must be fully fenced with a locking gate, or have a locking cover. Above-ground needs a tip-up/removable ladder or full fencing.
  • Ponds: need a life ring tied to an immovable object. (Lakes are exempt from this requirement.)
  • Trampolines: need proper netting or a fully fenced yard.
  • Roofs: must be under 20 years old or within manufacturer lifespan. Unapproved roofing: untreated wood boards, metal-over-shingle, 3+ layers of shingles, anything over 20 years. Roofs 15+ years old need documentation of age; if not provided, a 2% of Coverage A deductible applies to wind/hail.
  • Underwriting will generally work with agents on a reasonable timeline to fix issues (junk removal, dead tree removal) rather than declining outright — except for clearly uninsurable risks (structural collapse, tarped roofs, chimneys pulling away from the house).
  • If a specific structure/feature is the problem (unusual outbuilding, unclear addition, outdoor shower, etc.), it can often be excluded from coverage rather than losing the whole sale.

RCT (Residential Component Technology) — Live Demo Notes

  • Full name is Residential Component Technology, not "Replacement Cost Tool."
  • Required inputs before RCT unlocks: year built, home style, number of families, number of stories, square footage.
  • Walk through room-by-room grade (Builders Grade / Custom / Semi-Custom) for kitchen and bathrooms — this materially affects value, so don't default it without asking.
  • Interior flooring types must total 100% (hardwood/carpet/vinyl/tile mix).
  • Door count and baseboard/molding size are asked but have minimal price impact — don't over-invest time counting doors.
  • Roof shape/pitch (gable/hip/flat, steep/moderate) and square footage of siding materials (vinyl vs. stone veneer, etc.) matter more.
  • After completing RCT: Calculate → Finish → Save/Close → Sync from RCT on the Dwelling Construction screen. Reconstruction cost carries over automatically once synced (don't manually estimate it first).
  • You cannot lower the RCT-calculated Coverage A value without underwriter approval; you CAN raise it (e.g., using Extended or Extended Premier Replacement Cost, or a manual increase) if the insured believes the home is worth more — document why in a policy note (e.g., "lender requires Coverage A of $X").
  • If a lender requires a specific Coverage A amount that's higher than what RCT calculated, note the lender requirement explicitly rather than just overriding the number.

Loss Evaluation Types — Quick Refresher (plain-language)

TypeWhat it means
Repair CostConventional materials, actual cash value basis — the "base" option
Replacement CostUp to 100% of insured value, like-kind-and-quality materials
Extended Replacement CostAdds 50% over Coverage A (was 25% before the 2025-ish enhancement)
Extended Premier Replacement CostAdds 100% over Coverage A (was 50% before)

Coverage D (Loss of Use) is Actual Loss Sustained for Special Form up to 12 months — not a hard dollar cap, but bounded by 20% of Coverage A as the practical ceiling since that's what typically gets funded.

Order of Operations — Binding a Multi-Policy Account

Always bind Membership → Auto → Home → Umbrella, in that order. Getting this wrong (e.g., binding Auto before Membership) breaks account-level billing setup and is described as an easy, common mistake.

  • Home and Umbrella need a policy number to cross-reference the Auto policy (and Umbrella needs both Auto + Home numbers). While quoting, use "TBD" as a placeholder for policies not yet bound, then go back and fill in the real numbers once each policy issues — otherwise the multi-policy discount can fall off.
  • Membership itself doesn't need to be quoted (flat ~$50), but must be bound first since it sets the payment method precedent for the whole Guidewire account.
  • Escrow-billed homes should go on their own separate Guidewire account (billing is account-level in Guidewire) — a home paid via mortgage escrow can't share an account with Auto/Umbrella that the insured pays directly. This is worth doing proactively/by default, since finding out about escrow after quoting everything on one account means starting over.

New Home Purchases — Timing Rules

  • Don't issue the policy more than 1–2 days before the actual closing date — once issued, policy terms can't be changed, and closing dates shift often.
  • You can quote 8+ days ahead to lock in the Advance Signing Discount — issuing can still happen close to the closing date and keep that discount, it just won't be effective until the actual 8-day mark.
  • Lenders need proof of coverage on a declarations page before closing. Use a Field Issued Dec or invoice if the policy isn't bound yet.

Lake Estate (Legacy) — Product Overview

  • Farm Bureau's differentiator — few if any other Michigan carriers offer a comparable lake-specific policy.
  • Eligibility: must live on a main lake or have deeded/direct frontage; must be a Farm Bureau member; owner-occupied. Qualifying water bodies: the four Great Lakes bordering Michigan, all natural and man-made inland lakes (ponds don't count), channels/canals connecting to a lake, and the three connecting rivers between Great Lakes (St. Mary's, St. Clair, Detroit River).
  • Not eligible: condos, mobile homes, renters, builder's risk — those stay on a standard Homeowners policy even if lakefront.
  • System being migrated from the legacy platform to Guidewire; as policies renew they convert automatically. Migration has produced some pricing/data errors agents are still cleaning up — expect higher-than-expected renewal quotes to show up and require a help-desk dig-in.
  • Multi-policy discount is 20% on Lake Estate / Country Estate vs. 15% on standard Homeowners — writing a lakefront property as a plain Homeowners policy to "save the client money" is a false economy; it actually costs them the extra 5% multi-policy discount and less coverage.

Lake Estate Coverage Highlights (new/enhanced vs. old Legacy)

ItemOld LegacyNew (Guidewire)
Additional Living Expense12 months24 months
Watercraft$2,000$20,000 (blanket, no scheduling required)
Trailers$2,000$10,000
Water damage~$10,000$25,000
Debris removal (landscape/trees/shrubs)lowerincreased significantly
Extended Replacement Cost25% of Coverage A50% of Coverage A
Extended Premier50% of Coverage A100% of Coverage A
Uninsured boaters—up to $50,000
Snowmobiles—up to $15,000
Water backup—starting at $5,000
  • Fuel spill liability and Uninsured Boaters/Watercraft Physical Damage endorsements are now automatically included (renamed from older endorsement names).
  • Boats need <250 horsepower for included liability coverage.
  • Seawalls, docks, piers, boat hoists, and ice shanties are all insurable. Deductible for seawalls/docks/piers/wharfs is a flat $250 (not tied to the homeowner's deductible).
  • A "seawall" must be actual constructed/man-made wall (concrete, etc.) — loose decorative rock along a shoreline does not qualify.
  • Permanent boat hoists/boathouses = Coverage B (Other Structures, since they're not removed seasonally). Removable/seasonal hoists, anchored docks, water trampolines = Coverage C (Personal Property), and don't need to be scheduled individually.
  • Flood insurance is not automatically required for a Lake Estate policy — a lake property can be outside a flood zone.

Country Estate / Farmowners — Quick Reference

  • System auto-classifies the policy type based on entered acreage/zoning info.
  • Country Estate: generally 2–160 acres; doesn't require agricultural income.
  • Farmowners eligibility: must have (or expect) farm income, farm acreage, farm personal property, and farm buildings; minimum 2 acres if zoned agricultural, or minimum 5 acres.
  • Farm/Country Estate policies also get the 20% multi-policy discount (vs. 15% standard Homeowners).
  • Farm specialists handle the sizing/classification (Farm sizes 1–6 based on scale) — loop them in rather than trying to quote complex farm risk solo.

Miscellaneous Coverage Clarifications from Q&A

  • Coverage C vs. Coverage A for appliances: even appliances that convey with a home sale (fridge, washer/dryer) are Coverage C (personal property), not Coverage A — they aren't permanently attached, and sellers aren't obligated to leave them.
  • Loss Assessment = coverage for when a shared/communal association (HOA, condo association) levies a special assessment on homeowners to cover damage to shared property (e.g., a community pool). Can be increased for HOA members; can be removed if the home isn't part of an association.
  • Solid fuel heat units (wood/pellet/corn stoves): $150 surcharge per unit, can't be the sole heat source, must be UL-approved with documented clearance from walls, requires Solid Fuel Stove Report (form 1412) submitted with the application, and requires interior photos.
  • Ting device (free wiring-monitoring device from FB): required on dwellings with Coverage A of $1M+ (one per primary electrical panel); required on $3M+ dwellings (one per panel, installed within 30 days of binding, photo verification not needed since FB can confirm installation remotely). Not required below $1M but offered free — no discount attached since FB provides it at no cost. Has caught ~70 wiring issues across ~14,000 devices deployed so far; also sends power-outage alerts.
  • Water shutoff device: required for dwellings $3M+ Coverage A; homeowner pays for it themselves, must install within 30 days of binding, and photo proof is required (unlike the Ting device).
  • Jewelry: any single piece valued $10,000+ requires an appraisal dated within the last 5 years. A collection of smaller pieces that only totals $10k+ (with no single piece over $10k) does not require appraisal, but each piece still needs to be listed/described separately (the 4 Cs — cut, clarity, color, carat). Very high-value pieces may be better placed with an FB Partner carrier rather than scheduled on the homeowners policy.
  • Watercraft SPA: need CC (engine size), storage location, year/make/model/serial number (serial not required to quote, but required to bind). Boat, motor, and trailer can each be scheduled/valued separately if the client wants itemized coverage, or bundled.
  • Builders Risk: effective date must be at construction start; dwelling must be completed and occupied within 12 months; automatically includes a Building Materials endorsement (up to 10% of Coverage A, max $100k) covering materials whether or not yet attached to the structure; named-perils theft coverage requires signs of forced entry; contractor's own tools/equipment are never covered (that's on the contractor's policy) — only the homeowner's own tools.

Source: Homeowners Product Guide, 2024 edition (PDF uploaded Aug 12, 2026)

By-Peril Rating

Section I – Property uses By-Peril rating (separate premium per peril, not one all-perils premium). 7 perils, each with its own base rate:

PerilExample
FireSmoke damage
TheftTheft of items
Water BackupWater backup flooding
Weather Non-WaterWind loss
Weather-WaterWind driven rain
Non-Weather WaterWater damage from burst pipe
OtherDebris removal, sinkhole collapse, mold, animal damage, lost pet expense, riot/civil commotion, earth movement

Territories

Rate off Census tracts (greater granularity, aligns with competitors). Broken out by the same by-peril structure.

Protection Class

Now assigned automatically by geocoding — agent doesn't need to assign manually. If it can't be pulled or a split class applies, system prompts questions. Only applies to the "Fire" peril. Protection Class 1 is now available (new addition).

CERP (Claims Experience Rating)

All HO/MHO policies rated on: prior claims experience (past 3 years) + policy longevity with Farm Bureau.

Prior claims experience sources: paid FB claims on existing/prior HO/MHO/LE policy; paid claims with another carrier per Property CLUE Report; prior paid claims self-reported by Named Insured.

Longevity: years of continuous active HO/MHO/LE policy with FB. Any inactivity >90 days resets to zero. Follows the Named Insured(s) to new/additional locations. A seasonal dwelling in a Trust/LLC name only may qualify if a trustee/member/manager has a primary dwelling insured with FB.

Chargeable vs. Non-Chargeable Claims

Non-chargeable if no payment made (reserve-only is non-chargeable).

Always non-chargeable loss causes (CLUE code in parens): Hail (HAIL), Lightning (LIGHT), Earth Movement (MOVE), Earthquake (QUAKE), Wind (WIND), Wind-Driven Rain/Ice, Weight of Ice/Snow, Food Spoilage (all WEATH).

Medical claims: chargeable only if tied to another chargeable injury-liability claim (dog bite, premises hazard, slip and fall, trampoline, act of insured, fire). Stand-alone medical or medical-with-wind = non-chargeable.

Other rules:

  • Select Plus/Premier Debris Removal for Landscape Trees/Shrubs/Plants claims (FB code "DR") = non-chargeable
  • Residence Glass = non-chargeable; Cyber Protection = chargeable; Underground Service Line = chargeable
  • Travel Trailer = non-chargeable; Mono-line SPA = non-chargeable; all other SPA = chargeable
  • Insured with ≤2 claims totaling <$1,000 paid = non-chargeable
  • Home Systems Protection claims: chargeable/non-chargeable determined by cause of loss
  • Multi-cause claims: non-chargeable if one of the non-chargeable causes is present; but if a Residence Glass or non-chargeable SPA cause combines with a chargeable (non-listed) cause, it's still chargeable
  • Adding a Named Insured requires a new CLUE report (except Trust/LLC policies); their chargeable claims get added to the policy at issuance
  • Farm/Dwelling Fire policy claims don't get a star (*) on CLUE and are non-chargeable
  • Disputed CLUE claims: insured must contact the carrier shown — FB cannot remove CLUE claims; documentation can be submitted to argue non-chargeable status

Discounts and Surcharges

Protective Devices Discount (GH 66 06 — added to policy when discount applied)

DeviceDiscount
Complete Local Burglar Alarm2%
Central Station Burglar Alarm5%
Central Station Fire Alarm5% (not available Mobile Home — rapid destruction risk)
Automatic Fire Sprinkler5% (must cover ≥75% of home)
Automatic Backup Generator2%
Battery Backup Sump Pump2%
Water Leak Detection System2%

Multiple devices = sum of discounts. Can be applied any time (new business, renewal, mid-term).

Documentation required:

  • Central alarm systems: certificate of installation showing system/monitoring type
  • Generator, sump backup, water leak detection: any of — install certificate, builder specs, appraisal, real estate listing, or purchase/install receipts, or photos of installed device
  • Missing documentation = discount removed for that item

Key definitions: Local burglar alarm needs U.L. approval + audible alarm (doorbell cameras don't qualify). Central station burglar = U.L. approved, signals police response. Central station fire = U.L./NFPA approved, signals fire dept.

Mature Insured Discount

Homeowners age (Named Insured or spouse)%
30–397%
40–4915%
50+30%

Mobile Homeowners: 30% flat if 50+. Auto-applies at renewal once birthdate on file; can also apply mid-term via policy change. Trust/LLC seasonal dwellings may qualify if a member/manager/trustee's primary dwelling is FB-insured (Underwriter approval needed).

New Home Discount

Homeowners: dwelling ≤30 years old. Mobile Homeowners: mobile-manufactured home ≤5 years old. Not available on Renters. See Rate Manual section PC-2006R for %.

Multi-Policy Discount

Individual%Combination%
Personal Auto15%Auto + Life18%
Life5%Auto + Commercial16%
Commercial3%Life + Commercial6%
Auto + Life + Commercial20%
  • Auto: requires active FB Personal Auto policy
  • Commercial: requires active FB Business Auto, Commercial Property Package, Commercial Fire, Commercial Inland Marine, General Liability, Guardian, Ag Workers Comp, Commercial Workers Comp, or Businessowners (ownership-interest based)
  • Life: requires qualifying FB Term ($250k+ total face value), Universal ($25k+ face), or Whole Life ($25k+ face) policy (owner-based; can be added at HO new business)
  • Trust/LLC seasonal dwellings may qualify per member/manager/trustee's primary dwelling — Underwriter approval needed

Roof Age Discount

Roofs 19 years or newer → automatic new roof credit. 20+ years → no discount. When "Roofing Upgraded" is selected in Guidewire on new HO/MHO policies, contractor documentation is no longer required. On renewals, the discount no longer displays as a line item, and "Roof Age Discount (Year Roof: XXX)" no longer prints on declarations.

FB Advantage Discount

Insurance score from consumer reporting agency. Requires full name (+ middle name), complete address, DOB for each Named Insured. Auto-rescored every 3 years at qualifying renewal; can request rescore every 12 months via E-form E-CS026 (only applied if score changes). New model impact: +0.0% overall, with a +/-5% cap on factor changes from rescoring (unwinds over multiple renewals).

Trust/LLC-only policies get "No Score/No Hit" factor, unless a qualifying member/manager/trustee relationship exists (husband/wife, siblings, or combination like parents+kids) AND that person's primary dwelling is FB-insured — Underwriter approval required.

SmartPay Discount

Up to 40% total, built from three components:

  1. Billing History — 3-year count of FB non-pay cancellations/pending cancellations/renewal lapses across HO + Auto on the same account
  2. Payment Method — EFT vs. non-EFT
  3. Payment Plan — installment frequency selected

Lien-Billed discount varies by insurance score: 1656+ gets full-pay-equivalent discount; lower scores are tiered lower. Determined automatically at new business/renewal. Full breakdown in Rate Manual PC-2006R.

Advance Signing Discount

DiscountMin Days Bound Before Effective DateMax Days
No discount02
3%37
10%860
No discount61+—

3–7 day tier: reduces 1%/year until longevity year 3, then discount drops entirely. 8–60 day tier: reduces 1%/year until longevity year 9, then holds at 1% indefinitely (while continuously in force).

Affinity Discount

Category% (pre-09/15/2024)% (effective 09/15/2024)
Alumni6%5%
Civic4%5%
MFB Network15%10%
Professional10%5%

Only the highest applicable discount applies if qualifying for multiple — best practice to still list all eligible associations. Named Insured (not just their employer) must hold the membership. Requires Affinity Discount Signature Form (form 2329), signed and uploaded to Guidewire at binding; proof of membership kept on file at agent's office (may need both sides of card). Military retirees: DD214, VA ID, or Veteran-designated driver's license accepted as proof.

Surcharge for Solid-Fuel Heat

"Solid fuel" = non-gaseous/non-liquid fuel (wood, coal, pellets, corn); in-wall fireplaces exempt. Must be disclosed — if properly installed/UW-accepted, it's surcharged. If undisclosed and a loss occurs: Special Deductible of 10% of loss (max $10,000) applies in addition to the normal deductible.

Primary dwelling: solid fuel as primary heat source = unacceptable (unless listed "Approved Heating System"). Supplemental units acceptable if: U.L./CSA/UL-1482-tested labeled, code-installed; Solid Fuel Stove Report (form 1412) submitted with new business or policy change; photos of unit/floor/wall protection/clearances/chimney venting uploaded; no heat exchangers (except coal units, if regularly cleaned).

Seasonal dwelling: primary solid-fuel heat requires UW prior approval; only qualifies for Broad Form + Repair Cost Loss Evaluation (Form 01).

Mobile Homeowners: unit must be factory-installed or manufactured/professionally installed for mobile home use; other units need UW approval.

Outside units: surcharge may be waived by UW based on distance from dwelling; must still be UL/CSA-approved or tested; units within 10' of any structure referred to UW.

Fireplace inserts: require UL-approved metal chimney the full length of the existing masonry chimney (photos required).

Other structures (garage etc.): not acceptable if combustibles/vehicles/gas equipment stored inside; otherwise same requirements as Primary Dwelling apply, with full interior photos required.

If it can't be pulled or a split class applies, system prompts questions. Only applies to the "Fire" peril. Protection Class 1 is now available (new addition). CERP (Claims Experience Rating) All HO/MHO policies rated on: prior claims experience (past 3 years) + policy longevity with Farm Bureau. Prior claims experience sources : paid FB claims on existing/prior HO/MHO/LE policy; paid claims with another carrier per Property CLUE Report; prior paid claims self-reported by Named Insured. Longevity : years of continuous active HO/MHO/LE policy with FB. Any inactivity >90 days resets to zero. Follows the Named Insured(s) to new/additional locations. A seasonal dwelling in a Trust/LLC name only may qualify if a trustee/member/manager has a primary dwelling insured with FB. Chargeable vs. Non-Chargeable Claims Non-chargeable if no payment made (reserve-only is non-chargeable). Always non-chargeable loss causes (CLUE code in parens): Hail (HAIL), Lightning (LIGHT), Earth Movement (MOVE), Earthquake (QUAKE), Wind (WIND), Wind-Driven Rain/Ice, Weight of Ice/Snow, Food Spoilage (all WEATH). Medical claims : chargeable only if tied to another chargeable injury-liability claim (dog bite, premises hazard, slip and fall, trampoline, act of insured, fire). Stand-alone medical or medical-with-wind = non-chargeable. Other rules : Select Plus/Premier Debris Removal for Landscape Trees/Shrubs/Plants claims (FB code "DR") = non-chargeable Residence Glass = non-chargeable; Cyber Protection = chargeable; Underground Service Line = chargeable Travel Trailer = non-chargeable; Mono-line SPA = non-chargeable; all other SPA = chargeable Insured with ≤2 claims totaling <$1,000 paid = non-chargeable Home Systems Protection claims: chargeable/non-chargeable determined by cause of loss Multi-cause claims: non-chargeable if one of the non-chargeable causes is present; but if a Residence Glass or non-chargeable SPA cause combines with a chargeable (non-listed) cause, it's still chargeable Adding a Named Insured requires a new CLUE report (except Trust/LLC policies); their chargeable claims get added to the policy at issuance Farm/Dwelling Fire policy claims don't get a star (*) on CLUE and are non-chargeable Disputed CLUE claims: insured must contact the carrier shown — FB cannot remove CLUE claims; documentation can be submitted to argue non-chargeable status Discounts and Surcharges Protective Devices Discount (GH 66 06 — added to policy when discount applied) Device Discount Complete Local Burglar Alarm 2% Central Station Burglar Alarm 5% Central Station Fire Alarm 5% (not available Mobile Home — rapid destruction risk) Automatic Fire Sprinkler 5% (must cover ≥75% of home) Automatic Backup Generator 2% Battery Backup Sump Pump 2% Water Leak Detection System 2% Multiple devices = sum of discounts. Can be applied any time (new business, renewal, mid-term). Documentation required: Central alarm systems: certificate of installation showing system/monitoring type Generator, sump backup, water leak detection: any of — install certificate, builder specs, appraisal, real estate listing, or purchase/install receipts, or photos of installed device Missing documentation = discount removed for that item Key definitions : Local burglar alarm needs U.L. approval + audible alarm (doorbell cameras don't qualify). Central station burglar = U.L. approved, signals police response. Central station fire = U.L./NFPA approved, signals fire dept. Mature Insured Discount Homeowners age (Named Insured or spouse) % 30–39 7% 40–49 15% 50+ 30% Mobile Homeowners: 30% flat if 50+. Auto-applies at renewal once birthdate on file; can also apply mid-term via policy change. Trust/LLC seasonal dwellings may qualify if a member/manager/trustee's primary dwelling is FB-insured (Underwriter approval needed). New Home Discount Homeowners: dwelling ≤30 years old. Mobile Homeowners: mobile-manufactured home ≤5 years old. Not available on Renters. See Rate Manual section PC-2006R for %. Multi-Policy Discount Individual % Combination % Personal Auto 15% Auto + Life 18% Life 5% Auto + Commercial 16% Commercial 3% Life + Commercial 6% Auto + Life + Commercial 20% Auto : requires active FB Personal Auto policy Commercial : requires active FB Business Auto, Commercial Property Package, Commercial Fire, Commercial Inland Marine, General Liability, Guardian, Ag Workers Comp, Commercial Workers Comp, or Businessowners (ownership-interest based) Life : requires qualifying FB Term ($250k+ total face value), Universal ($25k+ face), or Whole Life ($25k+ face) policy (owner-based; can be added at HO new business) Trust/LLC seasonal dwellings may qualify per member/manager/trustee's primary dwelling — Underwriter approval needed Roof Age Discount Roofs 19 years or newer → automatic new roof credit. 20+ years → no discount. When "Roofing Upgraded" is selected in Guidewire on new HO/MHO policies, contractor documentation is no longer required. On renewals, the discount no longer displays as a line item, and "Roof Age Discount (Year Roof: XXX)" no longer prints on declarations. FB Advantage Discount Insurance score from consumer reporting agency. Requires full name (+ middle name), complete address, DOB for each Named Insured. Auto-rescored every 3 years at qualifying renewal; can request rescore every 12 months via E-form E-CS026 (only applied if score changes). New model impact: +0.0% overall, with a +/-5% cap on factor changes from rescoring (unwinds over multiple renewals). Trust/LLC-only policies get "No Score/No Hit" factor, unless a qualifying member/manager/trustee relationship exists (husband/wife, siblings, or combination like parents+kids) AND that person's primary dwelling is FB-insured — Underwriter approval required. SmartPay Discount Up to 40% total, built from three components: Billing History — 3-year count of FB non-pay cancellations/pending cancellations/renewal lapses across HO + Auto on the same account Payment Method — EFT vs. non-EFT Payment Plan — installment frequency selected Lien-Billed discount varies by insurance score: 1656+ gets full-pay-equivalent discount; lower scores are tiered lower. Determined automatically at new business/renewal. Full breakdown in Rate Manual PC-2006R. Advance Signing Discount Discount Min Days Bound Before Effective Date Max Days No discount 0 2 3% 3 7 10% 8 60 No discount 61+ — 3–7 day tier: reduces 1%/year until longevity year 3, then discount drops entirely. 8–60 day tier: reduces 1%/year until longevity year 9, then holds at 1% indefinitely (while continuously in force). Affinity Discount Category % (pre-09/15/2024) % (effective 09/15/2024) Alumni 6% 5% Civic 4% 5% MFB Network 15% 10% Professional 10% 5% Only the highest applicable discount applies if qualifying for multiple — best practice to still list all eligible associations. Named Insured (not just their employer) must hold the membership. Requires Affinity Discount Signature Form (form 2329), signed and uploaded to Guidewire at binding; proof of membership kept on file at agent's office (may need both sides of card). Military retirees: DD214, VA ID, or Veteran-designated driver's license accepted as proof. Surcharge for Solid-Fuel Heat "Solid fuel" = non-gaseous/non-liquid fuel (wood, coal, pellets, corn); in-wall fireplaces exempt. Must be disclosed — if properly installed/UW-accepted, it's surcharged. If undisclosed and a loss occurs : Special Deductible of 10% of loss (max $10,000) applies in addition to the normal deductible. Primary dwelling : solid fuel as primary heat source = unacceptable (unless listed "Approved Heating System"). Supplemental units acceptable if: U.L./CSA/UL-1482-tested labeled, code-installed; Solid Fuel Stove Report (form 1412) submitted with new business or policy change; photos of unit/floor/wall protection/clearances/chimney venting uploaded; no heat exchangers (except coal units, if regularly cleaned). Seasonal dwelling : primary solid-fuel heat requires UW prior approval; only qualifies for Broad Form + Repair Cost Loss Evaluation (Form 01). Mobile Homeowners : unit must be factory-installed or manufactured/professionally installed for mobile home use; other units need UW approval. Outside units : surcharge may be waived by UW based on distance from dwelling; must still be UL/CSA-approved or tested; units within 10' of any structure referred to UW. Fireplace inserts : require UL-approved metal chimney the full length of the existing masonry chimney (photos required). Other structures (garage etc.): not acceptable if combustibles/vehicles/gas equipment stored inside; otherwise same requirements as Primary Dwelling apply, with full interior photos required.
