notes.h:
Source: Coverage training, Aug 7, 2026

Michigan No-Fault Basics

Pays medical, wage loss, replacement services, property damage — regardless of fault. Replacement services examples: lawn care, wheelchair ramp/widening.

PIP limit options:

  1. Unlimited (default recommendation)
  2. Up to $500,000
  3. Up to $250,000
  4. Coordinated with health insurance ($2,500 limit)
  5. Medicaid ($50,000 limit)
  6. Medicare (older insureds)

PIP Selection & Deductibles

  • Primary = Farm Bureau pays medical first. Coordinated/excess = health insurance pays first (needs QHC letter every renewal)
  • $1,000 deductible = 19% discount; minimal savings past $1,000
    • Strategy: apply the auto deductible to a hospital bill, then submit to health insurance to satisfy both deductibles at once
  • Opting out (options 4–6) requires: PIP selection form (signed every renewal) + QHC letter listing household + health plan covers auto accidents primary + individual deductible under $6,579

Bodily Injury / UM/UIM

  • BI defaults 250/500, up to ~$1M/$1M
  • Umbrella requires BI at 500/500 minimum
  • Going below 250/500 needs a signed form every renewal (if not returned, renews at unlimited)
  • UM/UIM optional but recommended — always match to BI limits. Covers hit-and-run too.
  • PPI (property protection): $1M/accident, in and outside MI — don't recommend reducing

Collision / Comprehensive / Endorsements

  • Comprehensive: ACV minus depreciation/deductible — theft, hail, glass, windstorm (not deer — that's collision)
  • Collision: Regular (pay deductible regardless of fault) / Broadened (only if at fault, pricier) / Limited (don't offer — no real coverage if at fault)
  • Replacement cost endorsement: vehicles ≤3 yrs old, original owner only, falls off at 3 yrs
  • Mini-tort: not at fault + has regular collision → can pursue up to $3,000 from at-fault party's insurer. Needs police report + dec page. Insured handles it, not the agent.
  • Custom furnishings endorsement: for permanent aftermarket mods (lift kits, plows, interior mods). Ask "did it come off the assembly line this way?"
  • Rideshare/delivery endorsement: covers the gap when app is on, no rider yet. Ask: "will any vehicle deliver people or property for a fee?"

Additional Built-In Coverages

  • Rental reimbursement: defaults $50/day (30 days) — recommend bumping to $100/day (market rate often $83+)
  • Roadside assistance: on by default with comp/collision — towing up to $300, lockout, gas. Use Farm Bureau's vetted tow list (Agent Tool → Claims/Towing/Roadside)
  • Transportation expense: up to $30/day, $900 max, for total theft rental
  • Travel interruption: breakdowns 100+ miles from home
  • Personal effects: up to $300 (fire/flood/theft)
  • Non-owned trailers: up to $1,500, built in
  • Newly acquired autos: 15-day auto coverage if any vehicle has comp/collision; 5 days if PLPD only ($250 deductible)

Discounts & Telematics

  • Smart Pay (EFT full-pay) = largest discount
  • Multi-policy/affinity: 5–10%
  • Advanced signing: push effective date 8+ days out = 10%, 3 days out = 3%
  • Drives Michigan (telematics): 10% annual / 8% semi-annual — flags >80mph, hard braking, phone use, time of day. Cannot raise premium; min benefit is 1%. Code expires in 30 days — activate promptly. Only one driver needs to enroll.
  • Always quote with telematics — skipping it puts Farm Bureau 10% behind competitors
  • Semi-annual: only write if a ticket/accident is about to fall off — annual is almost always better

Quick Reference — Questions to Ask

  • "Did it come off the assembly line this way?" (custom furnishings)
  • "Will any vehicle be used to deliver people or property for a fee?" (rideshare)
  • "How did you find us?" (marketing attribution — carries over from sales playbook)

Added from: Aug 7 system/product training

Membership Requirement

  • $50/year membership required to write ANY auto policy — not required for standalone home or life
  • Regular (ag-involved, voting rights) vs Associate — same $50 either way
  • Membership perks: hotel discounts, $500 off Ford, John Deere/Caterpillar/Yamaha discounts, Great Wolf Lodge (30%), rental cars (20%), Detroit Zoo — often worth more than the $50 fee

PIP Options — Full Detail

  1. Unlimited (default/recommended)
  2. Up to $500,000
  3. Up to $250,000
  4. Coordinated with health insurance ($2,500 limit) — needs QHC letter + PIP selection form every renewal; individual deductible must be under $6,579
  5. Medicaid ($50,000 limit)
  6. Medicare (older insureds)
  • Unlimited PIP covers: replacement services, wage loss, survivor loss, attendant care, one-time funeral payment
  • Deductible strategy: apply the auto deductible to a hospital bill, then submit that same bill to health insurance to satisfy both deductibles at once; FSA/HSA can reimburse it too

Affinity Discounts (5%, don't stack — use whichever is easiest to prove)

  • 4-year university diploma, professional/hobby orgs (Ducks Unlimited, Moose Lodge, etc.)
  • Farm Bureau employees/agents get 10% automatically — always better than stacking a 5%, don't bother
  • Must be Primary Named Insured or spouse; needs signed form + proof

Rate Stabilization (auto only)

  • If FB isn't competitive against Auto-Owners, Citizens, Pioneer, Frankenmuth, Fremont, or Hastings — submit their fresh quote (within 30 days) or renewal dec page to underwriting for an adjustment (officially "rate stabilization," not "matching")
  • Turnaround ~48 hours
  • Qualifications: 0 SERP points, no at-fault accident points, ≤2 conviction points/driver, FB Advantage score 1500–1997

Accident/Violation Surcharge Timelines

  • Farm Bureau: 3 years then falls off (varies by carrier elsewhere — AAA is 5 years, Farmers 3–5 depending on type)
  • Ask about accidents/tickets in the last 36 months during fact-find; pull the losses report at quote time — MVR only pulled after they commit (MVRs cost ~$15 each)

Endorsements — Additional Detail

  • Replacement cost endorsement: vehicle ≤3 years old AND original owner (lease buyouts don't qualify — you're the 2nd owner)
  • Mini-tort: not-at-fault + regular collision → client can pursue up to $3,000 from the at-fault party's insurer directly. Needs police report + dec page — client handles it, not guaranteed, no recourse if at-fault party is uninsured
  • Custom furnishings: permanent aftermarket mods only (lift kits, plows, headache racks, wheelchair conversions). Key question: "did it come off the assembly line this way?"
  • Broadened other auto: covers personal use of a company car you don't own
  • Rideshare/delivery: covers the gap when the app is on but no passenger/delivery is active. Key question: "will any vehicle be used to deliver people or property for a fee?"
  • Travel interruption: breakdowns 100+ miles from home
  • Transportation expense: up to $30/day, $900 max — rental specifically for total theft
  • Personal effects: up to $300, fire/flood/theft
  • Non-owned trailers: up to $1,500, built in automatically
  • Newly acquired autos: 15-day auto coverage if any vehicle on the policy has comp/collision; only 5 days + $250 deductible if the policy is PLPD-only
  • Wood burning stoves: need photos showing clearance from walls/floor plate; some detached structures with wood stoves may be ineligible/excluded entirely — ~$150 surcharge when eligible

Rental Reimbursement & Roadside

  • Rental reimbursement defaults $50/day (30-day max) — recommend bumping to $100/day; local rental rates often run $83+/day
  • Roadside assistance defaults ON with comp/collision; towing covered up to $300/incident. Off by default on PLPD-only, can be added back
  • Use FB's vetted tow provider list (Agent Tool Shed → Claims/Towing/Roadside) — non-vetted tow companies can charge unregulated rates; client pays upfront, FB reimburses

Salesforce Basics

  • Lead = minimal info (name, maybe phone/address) — like a business card
  • Account = has DOB and wants a quote — go straight to Account if they say "yes, quote me," skip the Lead step
  • Opportunity = active sales opportunity once quoting begins
  • Household = auto-groups people at the same address once policies are issued — no manual work
  • Project 300 list: list spouses on separate lines (a "300" list of couples is really only 150 households); no dashes in phone numbers; use legal names, not nicknames
  • Records aren't exclusive pre-bind — other agents can have the same lead in their system until a policy is actually written

Guidewire vs. Legacy System

  • In Guidewire: personal auto, home, lake estate (newly converted), mobile/manufactured home, condo, renters, builders risk, personal & farm umbrella, business owners policy, commercial package, commercial umbrella
  • Still on legacy system: farm owners policies, business auto policy (BAP), workers comp, country estates
  • Client transfers between agents must be client-initiated — agents cannot solicit or service another agent's existing client, even for a different product line

IT / Phishing Policy

  • 5 failed phishing tests within a rolling 12-month period = system access terminated (escalation meetings after 3rd and 4th fail)
  • Report suspicious emails via the "hook" icon in Outlook — when in doubt, report; a false-alarm report is never held against you

New Submission Workflow

  1. Create PNI, ANI, and drivers in Salesforce first (via LUBC) — Quickfill results aren't always accurate and can create duplicate accounts
  2. Guidewire: Account → Actions → New Submission → set effective date → select Personal Auto
  3. Error "product no longer available" = Account Holder changed off your original contact. Fix: Contacts tab → "Change Account Holder To" → select correct contact (search Address Book first to avoid duplicates)

Qualification Screen

  • Complete all questions — a disqualifying answer triggers a hard stop, can't proceed

Policy Info Screen

  • Order QuickFill Report here (still create contacts in Salesforce first per best practice)
  • Additional Named Insureds: must exist at Account level first → Add → Existing Additional Named Insured
  • FB Advantage Score: must be retrieved before leaving this screen if not already on file
  • Multi-Policy Discounts: mark Yes + policy number (a PA submission # works temporarily for HO multi-policy, but must be in force by issuance)
  • Billing History / Advance Signing Days: display-only, auto-calculated

Drivers Screen

  • Add driver: must exist at Account level first → Add → Existing Driver
  • Roles tab: relationship to PNI + all PIP info lives here
  • Affinity Discount: needs proof documentation on file
  • Retrieve Loss Report: required for every driver
  • Retrieve MVR: only after quote is done and client commits to buying — don't run early
  • Retrieve Coverage Verifier Report: confirms prior coverage on file
  • Telematics/FB Drives Michigan: only addable at new business or renewal, never mid-term; needs a phone number on file; insured has 30 days post-bind to activate or loses the discount

Vehicles Screen

  • Create Vehicle → enter VIN → VIN Search (auto-populates make/model/rating symbols)
  • Each vehicle needs a Principal Driver; a 2nd driver on the same vehicle must be Occasional
  • Answer "used to carry/deliver for a fee" — see TNC/Delivery section below
  • Additional Interest (lienholder etc.) must be added at Account level first, then selected on the vehicle
  • Vehicle Rate Modifiers: anti-theft device, multi-auto, work loss benefits waiver, etc.

Vehicle not found in Guidewire (pre-1981 or brand-new models)

  1. Create Vehicle → VIN Search returns "VIN not found"
  2. Copy the VIN, delete it from the field, click outside, paste it back
  3. Select Vehicle Type + Model Year manually
  4. "New model year VIN not found, use previous model year to find rating symbols?" → leave Yes unless no data comes back at all
  5. Check the Override VIN Search box, fill in Make/Model/Subtype — rating symbols should auto-populate
  6. If they don't, an Agent Assigned Symbol (Cost New value) may be required

Maximum Value endorsement

  • Only for vehicles 9+ model years old, only if current value (less depreciation) exceeds original cost new
  • Underwriting approval required for values entered over $20,000

PA Coverages Screen

Four tabs: Coverages (applied to all vehicles + per vehicle) → Other Coverages → Exclusions and Conditions → Modifiers (read-only summary of discounts/surcharges applied)

Risk Analysis → Quote → Issue

  1. Request Underwriting Approval if flagged (add notes — makes review faster)
  2. Run Validations before issuing — surfaces anything still missing
  3. Print Quote for a client copy (also saves to Documents)
  4. Payment screen: after membership binds, re-toggle between payment options to pull the updated info in before issuing
  5. Signed application required (DocuSign accepted) — upload as Document Type "PC Application," Sub Type "Eligibility/Signature"
  6. Bind Options → Issue Policy

Mid-Term Policy Changes

  1. Actions → Change Policy → set effective date
  2. Risk Analysis tab → Policy Change → Add the change type — this appears on the client's cover letter (the free-text description field does not print, but is good practice for internal notes)
  3. Missing a Policy Change Type won't block quoting, but will hard-stop issuance
  4. Quote → Issue Policy

Applying a change to the renewal

After issuing to the current term, a bolded link appears to apply the same change to the upcoming renewal. You must click it — the change does not carry over automatically otherwise.

Copy Submission

  • Only works on bound, withdrawn, or expired transactions — not available for renewals or policy changes
  • Any expired reports get re-run automatically: FB Advantage Score expires after 90 days, MVR/Loss reports after 30 days, quotes after 30 days (still usable for copying). Quickfill does not need to be re-run.

Out-of-Sequence Changes

Happens when a transaction's effective date is earlier than the last completed transaction's date.

  1. Process the earlier-dated change — system flags it as out-of-sequence
  2. If both changes touch the same field, resolve via the Policy Review tab (override yes/no per conflicting item)
  3. After both transactions complete, process a 3rd blank ($0 premium change) policy change dated the same as the last bound transaction — this is what makes the declarations reflect the full current state. Skipping this step means the client never gets an accurate up-to-date dec page.
  4. Always leave a note describing what changed on out-of-sequence work — it's confusing to reconstruct later without one

Quickfill Reasons Not Added

Use Not in Household / Deceased / Former Resident to bypass bad or irrelevant Quickfill records — never select a driver/vehicle with incorrect info, it creates bad contacts. Quickfill must be ordered every quote (right after qualification), but the results don't have to be used.

Risk Analysis Report Checklist

  • UW Referral — blockers/informational messages, request approval here
  • Coverage Verifier — valid prior insurance within the last 14 days
  • Prior Losses — 2+ at-fault accidents in 3 years = ineligible for a PA policy
  • MVR — verify name spelling and DOB match
  • FB Advantage Score — confirm a score returned for every named insured
  • PA Underwriting direct line: (517) 580-6848

TNC / Delivery Endorsement

On the vehicle: "used to carry/deliver persons or property for a fee?" → Yes → select Network:

  • Delivery (UberEats, DoorDash, Grubhub, Shipt, Instacart, USPS/newspaper) — Primary Use must be Business, minimum 7,500 annual mileage (lower requires UW approval)
  • Transportation/TNC (Uber, Lyft) — Primary Use must be Business, no minimum mileage
  • Both can be selected on the same vehicle
  • Under Assign Drivers to Vehicles, check the Contracted Driver box for whoever's actually driving for the platform (multiple drivers can be checked)

Source: Kyle's training, Aug 10, 2026

Core Philosophy

  • Sell peace of mind, not a policy — coverage gaps sell themselves once explained
  • "If I'm going to give you business, you're going to at least give me a chance to quote yours"
  • "I don't care about price, I care about coverages"

Prospecting: Diversify to 7–10 Channels

No single channel failure should kill the pipeline.

  1. Lenders / Real estate — meet weekly from day one, relationship-first (ask about their kids/business, not just referrals)
  2. Chamber of Commerce — biggest single channel. Attend both monthly events, grab every business card, handwrite thank-yous, sponsor events
  3. Sponsorships — Farm Bureau AD co-op (~$1,450 your share, banner in school 5 yrs). Contact athletic director + principal. Popcorn bags via Gordon Food Service + local print co. stickers (~$1,200/5,000 bags)
  4. Google Leads — Farm Bureau setup ~$150. Budget $50–200/month, ~$10/click. Keep Google reviews coming in
  5. Texts + Mailers
    • Lead lists from DataMan (~$1,000/yr), timed to hit 1 month before renewal
    • ~1,600 mailers/month (~$700–800) — one farm policy pays for a year of mailers
    • Follow up with texts weeks 2, 3, 4 after mailers
    • texting.biz ($35/mo) — CSV import, mass text 300–400 at once, built-in opt-out compliance. Set up on desktop, not the call-forwarding app.
  6. Community / social — branded duck campaign (20/month), "Fueling Up the Community" gas card drop, Community Hero nominations
  7. Events / giveaways — QR code → Google/Microsoft form (name, address, phone, current client Y/N) + contact disclaimer. Follow up with everyone who entered, not just winners.

Always ask "how did you find us?" — tells you where to invest.

First Appointment (Phone — Fact Finding, ~15 min)

Goal: complete Farm Bureau fact-finding sheet + lock the in-person appointment.

  1. Auto — cars, drivers, kids, spell names correctly (verify legal names)
  2. Home — basic dwelling info
  3. Liability (most underinsured area)
    • "One of your most important coverages is liability — has anyone explained why?"
    • MI is no-fault, but they can still be sued for everything: house, cars, 401k, pension, 25% wage garnishment for 10 yrs
    • "What would your net worth be?" — brackets if they hesitate: 0–250k / 250–500k / 500k–1M / 1M+
    • Ask income separately: "How much do you guys roughly make?" (store for life insurance conversation)
  4. Life insurance (brief)
    • Skip "do you have it through work" — creates objections
    • Ask: "I'm sure you already have life insurance through work — do you own any outside of work?"
    • Leave the full conversation for in-person
  5. Get deck pages while still on the phone — "I don't care about price, black it out, I care about coverages"
  6. Set the in-person time before hanging up — never ask "what time works for you." Propose a specific time.

In-Person Appointment (Presentation)

  • Everything pre-filled before arriving — only signatures left. Bring life applications too.
  • Print deck pages, highlight every gap in orange/red
  • "I always like going over your current coverage first, then what we're proposing"
  • Walk every highlighted gap → "Everything I just addressed, I've fixed in ours"
  • Price last. State it, then stop talking. Wait 30–45 sec.
  • Close: "The only three things I need: signatures here, here, here — payment on this date — and you'd call to cancel your current carrier"
  • Wet signature or DocuSign on the spot; portable printer for on-site changes

Touches per person: postcard → text → follow-up texts (3–5 total) → repeat next year if no response

Life Insurance Process

  • Pivot after P&C signs: "I briefly mentioned life on the phone — would you be okay if I took you through a quick synopsis?" (never had a no)
  • LIFE diagram — let them build their own number: Loans / Income / Fixed expenses / Everything else
  • Never quote life pricing day-of — it's health-dependent
  • Follow-up plans: A = 4% of gross income (mostly permanent), B = 3% (mixed), C = 2% (mostly term). Quote spouses combined.
  • Kids: frame as a gift + insurability lock-in
  • Underwriting: <$500k = Right Life (instant, but audits exist), <$2M = height/weight/blood/urine, >$2M = EKG required
  • Follow up every other day through underwriting — post blood draw, close rate ~90%

Reminders

  • Research competitor rate increases (public record via state filings) — use in presentations
  • Start hiring search early — one extra household/month from a hire covers the cost under NATP

Added from: Culture panel (Matt Swab/Kyle Lott) + Natural Market training, Aug 3 & 6, 2026

Natural Market Strategy

  • Why start here: established relationship, trust, patience, support already exist
  • Reframe: 90% of the people you sit with have wrong/inadequate insurance — you're "throwing lifelines," not peddling policies
  • Build a list toward ~1,000 names (start with whatever you have, even 200–300)
  • Goal: 100% of your list knows what you're doing within one week — mix of calls, texts, face-to-face, social media

Asking for Introductions (Referral Script)

3 steps: (1) be introducible — act as a trusted advisor, not transactional. (2) ask — build it into the standard process, every time. (3) make it a system, not a one-off.

  • Script at the end of a coverage review: "The good news is we solved that. The bad news — 90% of the people I sit with have this same problem. Your mom, dad, brother, sister probably do too. Do your [sister] a favor — shoot her a text right now letting her know I'll be calling."
  • "Implied credibility" — a warm intro carries trust before you've even spoken. This is the single highest-converting channel described in training.
  • Script it out 5–10 times, practice out loud until automatic — ~30 days to build the habit, and habits are much harder to start late than early.

Centers of Influence (COIs)

  • Best sources: mortgage brokers/lenders, real estate agents, condo/HOA management companies, other insurance agents (especially life-only agents, or ones who don't write commercial/farm), accountants
  • Approach by giving, not asking: "I'm new, I want to learn your niche so I know who to send your way" — not "send me your leads"
  • Food chain logic: consumer → real estate agent → mortgage broker → you (you guarantee the money)

Cold Calling

  • Not a long-term strategy, but useful early to build activity while other channels ramp up
  • 20 dials/day is a sustainable daily commitment
  • Stop leaving voicemails if you're getting zero callbacks — focus effort on live answers
  • Select neighborhoods visually (well-kept homes = likely better insurance/credit risk) rather than buying "shopper" internet lead lists, which skew toward price-only habitual switchers

Door Knocking (integrated, not random)

  • Don't cold-knock a neighborhood blind — knock the neighbors of a client you're already visiting that day
  • Tell the client (don't ask permission) you're going to introduce yourself next door and leave a card: "Heaven forbid anything happens to your home, call 911 first, then call me second."
  • At the neighbor's door: "I just came from the [Name] next door — I'm their agent. Would you mind putting my card on your fridge? I'd be happy to give you a free second look." Implied credibility carries the conversation.
  • Best timing: after 6pm or Saturday mornings (dual-income households). In winter, ask the client for the neighbor's number and call instead of knocking.

Social Media

  • Facebook at minimum; LinkedIn/Instagram optional
  • Most posts should humanize you (family, community, shouting out local businesses) — insurance content sprinkled in occasionally, not constantly
  • Company Hootsuite version connects multiple platforms — signup link arrives ~48 hrs after setup, check spam folder, use FBInsMI email as username

Project 13 / Letter Campaign

  • Build a list of 1,300 names, mail 100/week for 13 weeks, then repeat (~4 touches/person/year)
  • Most effective version: hand-addressed white envelope, real stamp, brief intro letter, sample quote, fridge magnet business card
  • Cheaper version: postcards + phone follow-up
  • Long game — expect zero response in the first quarter, gradual traction after

LIFE Conversation Script (P&C → Life pivot)

  • Ask permission: "I briefly mentioned life on the phone — I take all my clients through a quick synopsis, would that be okay?"
  • L.I.F.E. = Loans, Income, Final expenses, Education — let the client build their own number out loud
  • Income is the biggest piece: multiply income × years until spouse/kids are financially independent
  • Never quote price the same day — it's underwriting-dependent
  • If they say "I'm all set," congratulate them, then still run the LIFE exercise to confirm

Liability Conversation Script

  • Use a real scenario (rear-ending someone who slams their brakes) to make the coverage gap emotionally real before naming a number
  • Ask them to guess the lawsuit amount themselves — creates internal pressure rather than agent-created pressure
  • Close with a trial-close summary: "Sounds like you feel [X] is inadequate and [Y] is more appropriate — did I hear that right?" — the client states the need, not you

Mindset Notes (from agency leader panel)

  • "Burn the boats" — no Plan B is repeatedly cited as the #1 differentiator between agents who make it and agents who don't
  • Reinvest early paychecks into the business rather than lifestyle upgrades
  • Start your hiring search in month 1–6 — licensing and training take longer than expected
  • Consistency beats motivation; the reward is delayed, not immediate
  • Always ask "how did you find us?" to know where to invest marketing dollars

Added: Aug 11, 2026

Property/Owner Lookup Tool — BS&A Online

When scouting a neighborhood to door-knock or mail, this is the way to pull owner names and addresses before you go.

  • URL (Deer Haven / your local municipality): https://bsaonline.com/PropertySearch/PropertySearchResults?SearchType=1&uid=494&SearchText=Deer+haven
  • This is BS&A Software's property records portal — used by most Michigan townships/counties for public assessing records. The uid=494 ties the link to a specific municipality; other townships will have a different uid, so bookmark separate links per area you prospect in.
  • Search by street name (or other search type) to pull a list of property owner names and addresses for that street
  • Requires a one-time human verification click on the site itself (a security checkbox) — this has to be done manually, it's not something to automate
  • Practical use: pairs directly with the door-knocking and Project 13 letter-campaign workflows above — pick a well-kept neighborhood, pull the owner list here, then either mail them or use it alongside the door-knock script when working a client's street

Attend both monthly events, grab every business card, handwrite thank-yous, sponsor events Sponsorships — Farm Bureau AD co-op (~$1,450 your share, banner in school 5 yrs). Contact athletic director + principal. Popcorn bags via Gordon Food Service + local print co. stickers (~$1,200/5,000 bags) Google Leads — Farm Bureau setup ~$150. Budget $50–200/month, ~$10/click. Keep Google reviews coming in Texts + Mailers Lead lists from DataMan (~$1,000/yr), timed to hit 1 month before renewal ~1,600 mailers/month (~$700–800) — one farm policy pays for a year of mailers Follow up with texts weeks 2, 3, 4 after mailers texting.biz ($35/mo) — CSV import, mass text 300–400 at once, built-in opt-out compliance. Set up on desktop, not the call-forwarding app. Community / social — branded duck campaign (20/month), "Fueling Up the Community" gas card drop, Community Hero nominations Events / giveaways — QR code → Google/Microsoft form (name, address, phone, current client Y/N) + contact disclaimer. Follow up with everyone who entered, not just winners. Always ask "how did you find us?" — tells you where to invest. First Appointment (Phone — Fact Finding, ~15 min) Goal: complete Farm Bureau fact-finding sheet + lock the in-person appointment. Auto — cars, drivers, kids, spell names correctly (verify legal names) Home — basic dwelling info Liability (most underinsured area) "One of your most important coverages is liability — has anyone explained why?" MI is no-fault, but they can still be sued for everything: house, cars, 401k, pension, 25% wage garnishment for 10 yrs "What would your net worth be?" — brackets if they hesitate: 0–250k / 250–500k / 500k–1M / 1M+ Ask income separately: "How much do you guys roughly make?" (store for life insurance conversation) Life insurance (brief) Skip "do you have it through work" — creates objections Ask: "I'm sure you already have life insurance through work — do you own any outside of work?" Leave the full conversation for in-person Get deck pages while still on the phone — "I don't care about price, black it out, I care about coverages" Set the in-person time before hanging up — never ask "what time works for you." Propose a specific time. In-Person Appointment (Presentation) Everything pre-filled before arriving — only signatures left. Bring life applications too. Print deck pages, highlight every gap in orange/red "I always like going over your current coverage first, then what we're proposing" Walk every highlighted gap → "Everything I just addressed, I've fixed in ours" Price last. State it, then stop talking. Wait 30–45 sec. Close: "The only three things I need: signatures here, here, here — payment on this date — and you'd call to cancel your current carrier" Wet signature or DocuSign on the spot; portable printer for on-site changes Touches per person: postcard → text → follow-up texts (3–5 total) → repeat next year if no response Life Insurance Process Pivot after P&C signs: "I briefly mentioned life on the phone — would you be okay if I took you through a quick synopsis?" (never had a no) LIFE diagram — let them build their own number: Loans / Income / Fixed expenses / Everything else Never quote life pricing day-of — it's health-dependent Follow-up plans: A = 4% of gross income (mostly permanent), B = 3% (mixed), C = 2% (mostly term). Quote spouses combined. Kids: frame as a gift + insurability lock-in Underwriting: <$500k = Right Life (instant, but audits exist), <$2M = height/weight/blood/urine, >$2M = EKG required Follow up every other day through underwriting — post blood draw, close rate ~90% Reminders Research competitor rate increases (public record via state filings) — use in presentations Start hiring search early — one extra household/month from a hire covers the cost under NATP Added from: Culture panel (Matt Swab/Kyle Lott) + Natural Market training, Aug 3 & 6, 2026 Natural Market Strategy Why start here: established relationship, trust, patience, support already exist Reframe: 90% of the people you sit with have wrong/inadequate insurance — you're "throwing lifelines," not peddling policies Build a list toward ~1,000 names (start with whatever you have, even 200–300) Goal: 100% of your list knows what you're doing within one week — mix of calls, texts, face-to-face, social media Asking for Introductions (Referral Script) 3 steps: (1) be introducible — act as a trusted advisor, not transactional. (2) ask — build it into the standard process, every time. (3) make it a system , not a one-off. Script at the end of a coverage review: "The good news is we solved that. The bad news — 90% of the people I sit with have this same problem. Your mom, dad, brother, sister probably do too. Do your [sister] a favor — shoot her a text right now letting her know I'll be calling." "Implied credibility" — a warm intro carries trust before you've even spoken. This is the single highest-converting channel described in training. Script it out 5–10 times, practice out loud until automatic — ~30 days to build the habit, and habits are much harder to start late than early. Centers of Influence (COIs) Best sources: mortgage brokers/lenders, real estate agents, condo/HOA management companies, other insurance agents (especially life-only agents, or ones who don't write commercial/farm), accountants Approach by giving, not asking : "I'm new, I want to learn your niche so I know who to send your way" — not "send me your leads" Food chain logic: consumer → real estate agent → mortgage broker → you (you guarantee the money) Cold Calling Not a long-term strategy, but useful early to build activity while other channels ramp up 20 dials/day is a sustainable daily commitment Stop leaving voicemails if you're getting zero callbacks — focus effort on live answers Select neighborhoods visually (well-kept homes = likely better insurance/credit risk) rather than buying "shopper" internet lead lists, which skew toward price-only habitual switchers Door Knocking (integrated, not random) Don't cold-knock a neighborhood blind — knock the neighbors of a client you're already visiting that day Tell the client (don't ask permission) you're going to introduce yourself next door and leave a card: "Heaven forbid anything happens to your home, call 911 first, then call me second." At the neighbor's door: "I just came from the [Name] next door — I'm their agent. Would you mind putting my card on your fridge? I'd be happy to give you a free second look." Implied credibility carries the conversation. Best timing: after 6pm or Saturday mornings (dual-income households). In winter, ask the client for the neighbor's number and call instead of knocking. Social Media Facebook at minimum; LinkedIn/Instagram optional Most posts should humanize you (family, community, shouting out local businesses) — insurance content sprinkled in occasionally, not constantly Company Hootsuite version connects multiple platforms — signup link arrives ~48 hrs after setup, check spam folder, use FBInsMI email as username Project 13 / Letter Campaign Build a list of 1,300 names, mail 100/week for 13 weeks, then repeat (~4 touches/person/year) Most effective version: hand-addressed white envelope, real stamp, brief intro letter, sample quote, fridge magnet business card Cheaper version: postcards + phone follow-up Long game — expect zero response in the first quarter, gradual traction after LIFE Conversation Script (P&C → Life pivot) Ask permission: "I briefly mentioned life on the phone — I take all my clients through a quick synopsis, would that be okay?" URL (Deer Haven / your local municipality): https://bsaonline.com/PropertySearch/PropertySearchResults?SearchType=1&uid=494&SearchText=Deer+haven This is BS&A Software's property records portal — used by most Michigan townships/counties for public assessing records. notes.t: PR, Listings, and Social Media Strategy
notes.path: PR, Listings, and Social Media Strategy.md
notes.h:
Source: Granola training recording, Aug 11, 2026 10:37 AM EDT

PR and Co-op Resources

  • Available: events, sponsorships, press releases, templates, listing/management consultations (Google, Apple Maps, directories), co-op tie-ins
  • American Me Essay Contest: ~60-year-old contest, free to participate — agents serve as local school contact, hand out certificates to top 3 winners per school. Good local PR (school visits, assemblies, parent exposure), no monetary cost, time commitment only.

Listings, Reviews, and Search Relevance

  • Consistent agency name across all platforms is critical — phone, email, address, name must match exactly everywhere (inconsistency creates separate data points, hurts search ranking)
  • Local search weighted by proximity, ratings, listing volume
  • Target 5–10 reviews to be competitive; reviews with a comment carry more weight than star-only
  • All 5-star profiles get more scrutiny — a 4.8 looks more legitimate
  • Start early reviews with confident customers, friends, family
  • Facebook business page and Google listing are the two most important review platforms
  • Respond quickly to all reviews/comments, including negative — take issues offline (call/email), don't discuss claims publicly

Social Media Strategy and Content Mix

  • Facebook business page is non-negotiable (personal pages can't run ads or use Hootsuite scheduling)
  • Content split (rough guideline): 50% general/conversational (Michigan lifestyle), 30% thought leadership (insurance explainers, law changes), 20% promotional (quotes, contests, announcements)
  • Algorithms deprioritize business content — staying off-topic most of the time improves reach
  • Pages lose relevance after 48–72 hours without activity; pre-schedule posts every 2–3 days
  • Most engaging content: personal and local (event photos, community involvement)
  • Video performs well, doesn't need to be polished; going live at events is high-engagement — verify accuracy before posting (Proofpoint can't screen video)

Growing Your Audience and Advertising

  • Encourage personal page followers to follow the business page
  • Join local Facebook groups, participate from the business page
  • Tag local businesses in posts — exposes page to their audience, can open commercial policy conversations
  • Facebook Ads offer best ROI for insurance social — target by zip code, age, income; start small ($5 test ads)
  • Boosting posts: useful when a post is already performing well; declining boosts temporarily reduces organic reach
  • Contest rules: no purchase/policy required to enter, no cash prizes (becomes a raffle under state law), gift cards/goods have dollar limits (Yeti coolers ~$200–500 are a common safe choice); use engagement prompts instead of follow/share requirements

Hootsuite and Proofpoint

  • Hootsuite: connects Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, etc. — content calendar, Amplify library (pre-approved Michigan content), consolidated inbox, analytics, AI post drafting (review carefully), Canva integration, phone app
  • Proofpoint Social Patrol: compliance layer, flags FINRA/FCC violations with suggested rewording — Zachary also receives a copy of flags

Agent Profile Page and Web Presence

  • Agent profile pages being set up now (contact: Matt Hendro / Matt Mahindra) — headshot, contact info, map, "Request a Quote" link
  • Use the profile-specific quote link (not general site link) so leads route to you
  • Bio defaults to generic placeholder — update with prior career background, communities/counties served, differentiators (2–3 paragraphs)
  • QR codes: graphic design team (marketingdesign@fbinsmi.com) can create them
  • Custom URL: register a clean domain (e.g. zachhayesagency.com) via Namecheap; Matt must redirect it in the backend

Action Items

  • Set up Facebook business page (tutorial link in Hootsuite follow-up email) — required before Hootsuite/ads
  • Link social platforms to Hootsuite and connect Proofpoint Social Patrol; download the phone app
  • Email Matt Hendro with updated bio, request social icons on profile page, discuss custom URL via Namecheap
  • Begin collecting early reviews on Facebook and Google — target 5–10, ask for comments not just stars

notes.path: Project 200 Lead List — Salesforce and BS&A Setup.md
notes.h:
Source: Granola training recording, Aug 11, 2026 2:40 PM EDT

Project 200 Overview

  • Project 200 (or 300, varies by region): list of everyone in your natural market
  • Family, friends, prior contacts = highest-quality first lead list
  • Goal: get it formatted, scrubbed, and uploaded into Salesforce

Excel Template and Formatting Rules

  • 26 columns available; only 5 fields are critical for scrubbing: first name, last name, address, phone number, date of birth
  • One person per row, one row per adult in the household
  • Couples: separate rows for each, so scrubbing catches policies under either name
  • Business leads: mark "person" or "business" in the "Lead and Referral Record Type" column — Zachary will split into two lists and upload separately
  • Business owner can also have a separate personal row (two distinct Salesforce records)
  • Submit as Excel only; PDF will be rejected and require resubmission

Submission Process

  • Search "Salesforce Lead List Import Request" in the directory (work unit)
  • Also accessible via Outlook (autofills when typing a new email) and Teams
  • Name the file with your name and agent number for tracking
  • Turnaround goal: 72 hours

Scrubbing Results and Error List

  • Green light: lead doesn't exist in system, or exists with no active policies in last 14 months
  • Red light: lead exists with active policies, or active within last 14 months
  • Error file returned after upload:
    • "Person account already exists, added to your team" = marketable, but won't appear under lead list; search manually in Salesforce
    • "Person account already exists" with another agent named = generally off-limits
    • Key phrase to watch: "Please reach out to the above agent" = do not pursue
  • First agent to write a policy on a lead becomes the owner; others lose access to market to that person
  • Leads with minimal info (last name only) still upload but won't be scrubbed until 5 key fields are added

BS&A Website for Additional Leads

  • Free public records site: look up addresses and properties by street or subdivision
  • Access: Barnyard > Agent Tool Shed > Business Internet Links > BS&A link
  • Oakland and Saginaw counties have a different process; BS&A less effective there
  • Export via Copilot on browser to Excel, or copy-paste manually
  • No phone numbers included; supplement with WhitePages or similar for cold calling
  • Submit exported addresses through the same Salesforce lead list import process
  • Tip: check home values and property details to qualify leads before outreach

Action Items

  • Submit Project 200 lead list to the Salesforce Lead List Import work unit (Excel file, name + agent number in filename); targeting end of day Wed Aug 12
  • Review error file returned after upload — flag any "please reach out to the above agent" entries before prospecting

notes.t: Farm Bureau Membership — County Contacts and Benefits
notes.path: Farm Bureau Membership — County Contacts and Benefits.md
notes.h:
Source: Granola training recording, Aug 11, 2026 12:47 PM EDT

County Farm Bureau Structure

  • 65 county farm bureaus statewide, each with a board of farmer members and a county administrator
  • CAMs (County Administrative Managers) are the primary ongoing contact for agents — also coordinate on inactive members whose policies may cancel without active membership
  • Contact info for each county included in the folder passed around

Membership Types and Pricing

  • Regular members: anyone involved in agriculture (full-time or part-time) — farmers, seed salesmen, livestock vets, local dealers, landowners renting to farmers. Get voting rights.
  • Associate members: anyone not involved in agriculture
  • $50 per family membership (covers a household; adults over 21 need a separate membership)
  • Agents can sell standalone memberships, no policy required

Why Members Join

  • Advocacy for agricultural issues, networking, savings through member benefits
  • Some join purely for advocacy — no insurance policy or farming connection needed

Member Benefits and Promotions

  • MFB Savings Marketplace (flagship): Walt Disney World, DoorDash, Kroger (5% off)
  • Ford: $500 cash reward on select vehicles via BlueAdvantage
  • Baywatch Resort (Traverse City): 20% off
  • Daycare discounts via MFB Savings Marketplace
  • Promoted via: Michigan Farm News, Seasonal Savings e-newsletter, Farm Gate blog, social media, Barnyard Bulletin, flyers/rack cards/brochures (BigCommerce), branded swag, in-person events
  • Flyers available on the website to print without waiting for marketing to send them

Tips for Agents

  • Get to know clients' pain points and match them to relevant benefits
  • Share stories of members using discounts
  • Multi-county agents: reach out to the relevant county CAM for each area (e.g., Taylor Sample for Allegan County)
  • General membership questions: Laura (back from vacation next week)

Action Items

  • Identify CAM contacts for counties served
  • Pull Farm Bureau membership business rules from the Barnyard

notes.h:
Source: Granola training recording, Aug 11, 2026 1:39 PM EDT ("education and support")

Training Program Overview

  • Onboarding runs 12–18 months total; 12 months if things go smoothly
  • Month 1: marketing day and field work; Month 2: rack review, comprehension check, commercial deep dive
  • Two advanced programs follow onboarding:
    • Trusted Advisor series: product deep dives, agent panels, underwriting/claims topics; timing guided by managing partners, some as early as 6 months in
    • Trustworthy Selling: 5-day external vendor program, held at 6–12 months in; covers buyer/seller psychology, prospecting, scripting, sales approach
  • Monthly continuing education webinars (Farm Bureau-specific, license renewal credit) — usually early in the month
  • License expiry varies by birthday: check renewal window carefully (1 or 2 years)

Agent Tool Shed Walkthrough

  • Barnyard = home office intranet; Tool Shed = field-facing subset for agents and staff
  • Access via the Tool Shed link in the red global barnyard toolbar
  • Top gray toolbar organized by line of business (membership, personal, life, commercial, agribusiness) — each page bundles product info, quoting resources, scripting, forms, support
  • Small screens: top toolbar collapses into a drop-down; narrow screens: right-side quick links move to bottom, alphabetically

Key Tool Shed Resources

  • Bulletins: internal field communications (rate changes, project launches, training announcements), kept 2 years then archived — review weekly
  • Guidewire Info Center: quoting platform resources (personal lines focus; life is separate)
  • Salesforce page: CRM resources, job aids, training links, videos (via FB Learning Center SSO)
  • Training Supply Center (TSC): one-stop training hub — links to FB Learning Center, shows upcoming training calendar and recorded sessions for missed live trainings

Supplementary Resources

  • FB Partners Group: inside brokerage for risks not eligible for Farm Bureau paper
  • Health Services: refer to subject matter experts
  • Sales and Distribution (formerly Marketing): Agency Management (hiring, marketing, prospecting, scripting), Education, Incentives (trip/award tracking), Brand and Digital Marketing
  • Print Shop and FB Learning Center also directly accessible from Tool Shed bottom links

Marketing Events and Next Steps

  • Handout covers Farm Bureau marketing events (trips, awards, seminars) — many 2026 events already passed; useful for planning 2027
  • Ask a mentor what events they attend and get out of them
  • Agent Business Seminar (ABS): upcoming, invitation likely coming — good for meeting agents, seeing event culture, includes 2027 marketing planning guide walkthrough

Action Items

  • Build weekly bulletin review into team meeting habits
  • Ask a mentor which marketing events they attend and why
  • Watch for Agent Business Seminar invitation

What B-File Does

  • Sends clients a 5-minute mobile-friendly risk assessment link to fill out on their own — easier than asking sensitive questions directly (income, 401k, savings)
  • Covers assets, liability exposure, life insurance, retirement values
  • Surfaces cross-sell opportunities: boats, motorcycles, umbrella, life, annuities

  • Response rate: 20–40% across prospects and existing clients (lower in summer)

Scheduling and Calling Services (Full Suite)

  • Full suite ($300/month): Household Intelligence link + live scheduling calls, up to 300 households — most new agents stay at this tier for 1–2 years
  • Link-only option: $100/month (no calling services)
  • Call types: new business thank-you, referral requests, P&C cross-sell follow-ups, re-quotes, win-backs, event leads
  • Billing starts October (not during training); reimbursable under the ~$4,800 first-year office expense allowance
  • Calendly recommended for scheduling — free version available, paid (~$11/month) unlocks workflows, text reminders, customization
  • B-File embeds the household intelligence link in Calendly confirmation emails so clients fill it out before appointments

  • Veteran agents use B-File heavily for annual renewal reviews; existing book of business drives growth over time
  • Average person holds 3 life policies over a lifetime — the recommendation starts the conversation even if full amount isn't purchased immediately
  • Annuity goal: one product per year currently, expected to increase; B-File data identifies who has liquid assets to target
  • Demo available via one-on-one call; B-File team will follow up by email toward end of training

Action Items

  • Set up a Calendly account (consider ~$11/month paid plan for workflows/reminders)
  • Watch for B-File team outreach email to schedule one-on-one demo

Source: Contracting day & training, Aug 3–7, 2026

Email Setup

  • Two formats issued: display email (firstname.lastname@fbinsmi.com) and login username (first initial + 6 letters of last name)
  • Use the login/username format to sign into all Farm Bureau systems — not the display email
  • Cash drawer number, office number, and agent number are all issued at setup — memorize your agent number, it's how you get paid
  • Password gets reset day-of with IT

Print Shop Voucher

  • $100 gift certificate from marketing for print shop orders (business cards, letterhead, envelopes, swag)
  • Must be used in a single order — orders under $100 may prompt an email asking if you want to add more
  • Headshots return ~Thu/Fri after contracting day; pick your favorite before ordering cards, or order without a photo first if you're in a hurry
  • Checkout note field: write "welcome voucher" to apply the $100

Solicitor License (Personal + Business)

  • Applied for via NIPR — business entity license requires your EIN, not your personal NPN/SSN
  • Only select: Accident, Health, Casualty, Life, Property — do not select Annuities (gets kicked back)
  • Business entity name = your agency LLC name; address must match your registered LLC filing address
  • Verification contact must be Courtney Cordes (ccordes@fbinsmi.com) — she tracks solicitor license status
  • Designated Responsible Producer = yourself (no other producers under your LLC yet)

Business Entity Licensing — DIFS Approval & Finalization

Source: Email from Lucy Carter (Marketing Field and Administrative Specialist), Aug 14, 2026

  • DIFS approved the business license (business resident producer license)
  • Next steps to finalize the business entity with Farm Bureau:
    1. Sign the LLC addendums — links are on page 2 of the "Business Resident Producer Licensing" document
    2. Sign using your exact business name (as registered)
    3. Verify banking info matches what's on file in ADP
  • Payroll will begin processing payments under the business entity starting September pay
  • DBA note: if advertising under any name that differs from the exact business name, a DBA must be filed with the state to stay compliant (separate instructions attached to Lucy's email)
  • Contact for questions: Lucy Carter, lcarte1@fbinsmi.com

Contract Signing Day

  • Signed via DocuSign inside the New Agent Onboarding Guide (Agent Tool Shed → Training Supply Center → Agent Training → New Agent Training Program)
  • Documents include: agent agreement, new agent development plan, agent beneficiary designation (need 2 beneficiaries' full legal info: name, DOB, SSN, address, phone, email)
  • Personal or Farm Bureau email both work for the DocuSign copy

Health Insurance & Payroll Benefits

  • 30-day window from enrollment date to elect/change health insurance (via Apollo) — next open enrollment is end of year, worth a calendar reminder
  • Automatic payroll deductions (not optional):
    • Long-term disability (~$24.90/mo, based on $36k default salary — adjustable each September)
    • Cyber protection (~$41.67/mo)
    • E&O (~$291.62/mo based on $1M coverage — increases as your book grows)

Prior Carrier Appointment Cancellations

  • All prior carrier appointments must be cancelled before the Farm Bureau appointment can finalize
  • Check status via NIPR by searching your own name — "active" appointments need to be called/cancelled; some carriers require a written letter, not just a call
  • Give it about a week after requesting — cancellations aren't instant

Teams & SharePoint Setup

  • Teams: add Farm Bureau email as a second account (don't replace your personal one)
  • Auto-enrolled SharePoint channels: Salesforce field support, Commercial Lines, Farm & Ag Business, Personal Lines, Document Center — post questions here, underwriters respond quickly
  • If not auto-enrolled: Agent Tool Shed → Training Supply Center (TSC) → Fields 14 → join manually

Hootsuite (Social Media Tool)

  • Skip the free public trial — a custom Farm Bureau version link arrives via email ~48 hrs after being added to the system
  • Check spam folder — the signup link can trigger spam filters
  • Use your FBInsMI email as the username when creating your password

  • The Barnyard = company-wide info portal
  • Agent Tool Shed (inside the Barnyard) = where you'll spend ~99% of your time — field-facing tools, product guides, job aids
  • FB Web Apps = password reset, phishing test dashboard ("Know B4")
  • Support tickets: email "support" with the issue — auto-routes to the right IT team, follow-up comes via Teams

Source: Commission structure training, Aug 4, 2026

Core Principle

  • Life insurance is baked into the contract deliberately — P&C-only agents make little; life-only agents make little; both together is where real income lives
  • Households with home + auto + umbrella + life have dramatically better retention (company-wide retention ~92%)

NADP (New Agent Development Program) — Launch Capital

  • $48,000 launch fund: 100% investment, not a loan — never repaid, doesn't come out of future commission
    • Paid monthly (20th of month): $4,000 × 3 months, then $3,000 × 3 months, then $2,000/mo until exhausted
    • E&O (~$291/mo) and cyber liability auto-deduct from this
  • $10,000 Business Accelerator Fund: discretionary, mainly for hiring staff — request it, prove ROI, request more
  • $1,500/month office stipend (agents housed in a veteran agent's office) — covers rent; if actual rent is less, the difference is yours for marketing
  • $6,000 Agent for Change grant: one-time, community-giving initiative (childhood hunger focus) if you don't already have a "thing" — can be split across multiple smaller grants (e.g. 3 schools × $2,000)

Commission Multiplier — 2.0x for First 20 Months

  • First 2 months are "freebie" months (heavy training, no scorecard pressure)
  • Multiplier locks at 2.0x for months 3–20 regardless of production pace
  • After month 20, multiplier is based on trailing production — front-loading production in year one matters

Tier System (New Agents)

  • Start at Tier 3 automatically
  • 12th placed life policy → moves to Tier 2
  • 24th placed life policy → moves to Tier 1 (locks in for the following year)
  • 24 life policies/year is repeatedly described as "table stakes"

Commission Rates (approximate, illustrative from training)

  • Base new-business commission ~10% blended (higher on niche/commercial, lower on standard personal lines)
  • Niche lines (commercial, ag, lake estate) get an added ~5.5% bonus once 3-year average production crosses certain thresholds
  • PC production bonus tiers kick in at $250k, $500k, $750k written
  • Renewal commission scales similarly — the gap between writing life insurance vs. not can be $120k+/year in renewal revenue on an identical-size book (~6% vs ~15% renewal rate)

Signature Award (first milestone)

  • Target by end of month 8 (month 6 of active NADP): 18 life policies + 60 P&C policies (umbrella counts as a P&C policy)
  • Reward: $500 check + recognition lunch with Nick Hurst (Senior State Sales Director)
  • Framed as "the floor," not the goal

All-American Trip Qualification

  • 2026 (this cohort's first partial year): 1 annuity required
  • Starting 2027: 2 annuities required
  • Two paths: 35 life policies + $11K commission, or 50 life policies + $9K commission
  • Given an August 2026 start, qualifying in 2026 is unlikely — 2027 is the realistic first target
  • Destination announced late September each year (past trips: Hawaii, Mediterranean cruise, Australia)

Long-Term Roadmap

  • Target: $2.5M book of business by end of NADP (~1,400 policies at ~$1,400 avg premium/policy, inflated by ongoing rate increases)
  • Early production pace strongly predicts which long-term "zone" (survive → Signature Award → thriving) an agent lands in

Mentor Program

  • Assigned mentor is local/geographic; you can also lean on any veteran agent, not just your assigned one
  • Company pays mentors a small commission for mentoring — no need to feel guilty reaching out
  • Zach's assigned mentor may be Ben Crooks — worth confirming directly, wasn't 100% certain in the training

Source: Leadership panel & onboarding kickoff, Aug 3, 2026

Core Philosophy

  • "You are in business for yourself, but you're not by yourself" — company, mentors, and fellow agents form a support system
  • Trusted advisor model: sit face-to-face, ask real questions, connect the dots for the client — don't sell over the phone or email
  • "Burn the boats" mentality — treat NADP capital like there's no Plan B, not a safety net

Why This Beats Transactional Selling (Matt Swab, 5-year agent)

  • Transactional (price-only) close ratio is low; trusted-advisor, in-person close ratio cited around 30–40%
  • Clients who understand why they need coverage stay loyal through rate increases — clients who bought on price alone leave the moment a cheaper quote appears

Reinvestment Mindset

  • Early on, pay yourself minimally and reinvest commission into branding, sponsorships, and eventually staff
  • Employee mindset: "I can't afford to hire someone." Entrepreneur mindset: "I can't afford NOT to hire someone."
  • Rule of thumb cited: one extra household/month from a new hire can cover their cost

Leadership / Key Contacts

  • CEO: Don Simon | President: Ben LaCrosse | Senior State Sales Director: Nick Hurst
  • West Region Managing Partners: Patrick Carpenter, Nate, Lauren Korfmacher, Morgan Shannon, Dev Wall, Sarah Becker
  • New MP (West): Ryan Mitten

Claims Philosophy (why it matters for the sales pitch)

  • Farm Bureau's claims dissatisfaction rate is cited internally as <0.01%
  • Adjusters proactively reach out to agents on sensitive claims (fatalities, major losses) — described as unusual compared to other carriers
  • Useful sales point: "I can tell you with full confidence, if something happens, we'll take care of you" — grounded in a genuinely strong claims reputation, not just a sales line
